On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Then We sent Our messengers in succession. Every time a nation's messenger came to it, they denied him, so We made some of them follow others, and We made them into tales. So away with a people who do not believe.﴾ (23:44)

Almighty God says: ﴿Then We sent﴾ to the nations which We brought into being after Thamud ﴿Our messengers in succession﴾, meaning: some of them following others, one after another. The word is derived from "tawatur" (successive occurrence), and it is a noun used as a plural, like "shay'" (thing). One does not say "jā'anī fulān tatarā" (so-and-so came to me in succession), just as one does not say "jā'anī fulān mawātiratan." It is written both with tanwin and without it, and it contains a yā'. Whoever does not give it tanwin reads it as "fa'lā" from "watara." Whoever says "tatarā" gives the impression that the yā' is original, as is said "mi'zan" with a yā' and "ma'zā," and "bahmā" with both, and similar forms. Thus it is sometimes given the inflection and sometimes left without it. Whoever takes it as "fa'lā" and pauses on it indicates the kasra; whoever takes the final alif as the alif of case-ending does not indicate it, because the alif of case-ending is not pronounced with a kasra. One does not say "ra'aytu Zaydan" and then indicate a kasra in it.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said regarding its interpretation.

Mention of those who said this:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Then We sent Our messengers in succession﴾: he said, they follow one another.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Then We sent Our messengers in succession﴾: he said, one after another.

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God: ﴿Tatra﴾: he said, one following another.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿Then We sent Our messengers in succession﴾: he said, one following another.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Then We sent Our messengers in succession﴾: he said, one after another, following one another.

The reciters of the regional centres differed in reading this. Some reciters of Makka, some of Madina, and some of Basra read ﴿tatran﴾ with tanwin. Some reciters of Makka, some of Madina, and most reciters of Kufa read it ﴿tatra﴾ with the yā' pronounced, in the pattern of ﴿fa'lā﴾. The position on this is that both are well-known readings and two recognised dialects of the Arabic language with one meaning, so whichever of them the reciter reads is correct. However, I myself prefer the reading without tanwin, because it is the more eloquent and more widely known of the two dialects.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Every time a nation's messenger came to it, they denied him﴾

He says: whenever a nation from those nations which We brought into being after Thamud received its messenger whom We sent to them, they denied him in what he brought them of the truth from Us.

* *

As for His words: ﴿So We made some of them follow others﴾

He says: We made some of those nations follow others in destruction, so We destroyed some of them one after another.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And We made them into tales﴾

for the people, and an example by which they are spoken of among the people. The word "aḥādīth" in this place is the plural of "uḥdūthah" (a tale), because the meaning is what you have described, that they were made into an example that people talk about. It is also permissible that it be the plural of "ḥadīth." It is said "wa-ja'alnāhum aḥādīth" because they were made into a tale and an example by which people are cited in evil; one does not say of good, "I made him a tale," nor "uḥdūthah."

* *

As for His words: ﴿So away with a people who do not believe﴾

He says: so God removed far away a people who do not believe in God and do not confirm His messenger.

* * *

And His words: ﴿And We sheltered them on a height﴾

He says: We gathered them together and placed them on a height. It is said: "So-and-so took refuge (awa) at a place such-and-such, so he takes refuge there (ya'wi ilayhi)," when he goes to it. And in the pattern of "af'altuhu," one says "fa-huwa yu'wihi" (he gives it shelter).

* * *

For this reason it is said of a man who is in a station of elevation among his people, and of honour, nobility and numbers: "He is on a height (rabwa) among his people." There are two readings of the word: rabwa with a damma on the ra' and with a kasra, when it is intended as a noun; and when it is intended as the verbal noun of the action, it is said: "raba, rabwa."

The people of ta'wil (interpretation, i.e. exegesis) differed about the place that God described with this attribute, to which He sheltered Mary and her son. Some of them said: it is ar-Ramlah in Palestine.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Safwan ibn Isa narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn Rafi narrated to us, saying: a paternal cousin of Abu Hurayrah, called Abu Abd Allah, narrated to me, saying: Abu Hurayrah said to us: "Keep to this ar-Ramlah of Palestine, for it is the height of which God said: ﴿And We sheltered them on a height, a place of settlement and a flowing spring.﴾"

* Isam ibn Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Abbad Abu Utbah al-Khawwas narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Amr ash-Shaybani narrated to us, from Ibn Wa'lah, from Kurayb, who said: "I do not know what..."

* Murrah al-Bahzi narrated to us, that he heard the Messenger of God ﷺ, and he mentioned that the rabwa is: ar-Ramlah.

* Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Bishr ibn Rafi, from Abu Abd Allah, the paternal cousin of Abu Hurayrah, who said: "I heard Abu Hurayrah say regarding God's words: ﴿to a height, a place of settlement and a flowing spring﴾: it is ar-Ramlah of Palestine."

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Safwan narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn Rafi narrated to us, saying: Abu Abd Allah, the paternal cousin of Abu Hurayrah, narrated to me, saying: Abu Hurayrah said to us: "Keep to this ar-Ramlah that is in Palestine, for it is the height of which God said: ﴿And We sheltered them on a height, a place of settlement and a flowing spring.﴾"

Others said: it is Damascus.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, that he said regarding this verse: ﴿And We sheltered them on a height, a place of settlement and a flowing spring﴾: "They claim that it is Damascus."

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: "It reached me, from Ibn al-Musayyib, that he said: Damascus."

* Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, the like of it.

* Yahya ibn Uthman ibn Salih as-Sahmi narrated to me, saying: Ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, regarding His words: ﴿And We sheltered them on a height, a place of settlement and a flowing spring﴾, he said: "To a height of the rubā of Egypt." He said: "There is no rubā except in Egypt, and when the water is released, the rubā are the places on which the villages stand; were it not for the rubā, those villages would be drowned."

Others said: it is Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem).

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: "It is Bayt al-Maqdis."

* He said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: "Ka'b used to say: Bayt al-Maqdis is closer to the heaven by eighteen miles."

* Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ka'b, the like of it.

The most fitting of these opinions as an interpretation of this is that it is a raised place with level ground, and visible water; and the attribute of ar-Ramlah is not like that, because ar-Ramlah has no flowing spring (ma'in) in it. And God, exalted is His remembrance, described this height as "a place of settlement and a flowing spring."

Some people of ta'wil have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And We sheltered them on a height﴾, he said: "The rabwa: the level one."

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿to a height﴾, he said: "Level."

The people of ta'wil said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

* Muhammad ibn Amarah al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿a place of settlement and a flowing spring﴾, he said: "The ma'in is water."

* Muhammad ibn Amarah al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "a flowing spring" – he said: "Water."

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn as-Salt narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Salim, from Sa'id, regarding His words: ﴿a place of settlement and a flowing spring﴾, he said: "A level place, and the ma'in is visible water."

* I was told by al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard ad-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿and a flowing spring﴾: "It is visible water."

Others said: by the qarar (settlement) He means the fruits.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿a place of settlement and a flowing spring﴾, "it has fruits, and it is Bayt al-Maqdis."

* Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, the like of it.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This statement of Qatadah regarding the meaning of ﴿a place of settlement﴾, even if he did not intend by his words that it is described as "a place of settlement" only because of the fruits in it, and because of that its inhabitants settle there, has no basis that we know of. As for ﴿ma'in﴾, it is a passive participle from "ʿintuhu, fa-anā uʿīnuhu" (I assist it), and it is mu'in; it may also be a fa'il form from "ma'ana, yamʿanu," so it is ma'in from al-ma'un (abundance), and from it is the saying of Ubayd ibn al-Abras:

A broken ravine, or a flowing spring that pours forth,
or a hill, before which are crevices.

[The verse is by Ubayd ibn al-Abras from his long rhyming qasida in bāʾ (Lisan: m-ʿ-n), which the author cited at the words of God, exalted: ﴿And We sheltered them on a height, a place of settlement and a flowing spring﴾. In Lisan al-Arab it says: al-Farra said: "dhat qarar" means level land. "Ma'in al-ma'" means visible, flowing water. He said: "You may make ma'in a passive participle from al-uyun (springs), (which the author preferred), and you may make it a fa'il from al-ma'un, whose root is al-ma'n. Al-ma'in is flowing water, and it was said: flowing over the surface of the earth, and it was said: sweet and abundant, and all of that is from ease. Al-ma'n is visible water." Al-luhub is the plural of lahb (with a kasra on the lam): the gap and the air between two mountains. In al-Muhkam: "mahra" is what is between every two mountains. It was said: it is the crack in a mountain, according to al-Lihyani. It was said: it is a small ravine in a mountain. It was said: it is a face of a mountain like a wall, which cannot be climbed. End of quotation.]

And God, exalted is His remembrance, described this height as "a place of settlement and a flowing spring."

Some people of ta'wil have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And We sheltered them on a height﴾, he said: "The rabwa: the level one."

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿to a height﴾, he said: "Level."

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* * *

And His words: ﴿a place of settlement and a flowing spring﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: among the attributes of the height to which We sheltered Mary and her son Jesus is that it is a flat, spacious land, with visible water, not hidden, flowing.

The people of ta'wil said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and a flowing spring﴾, he said: "The ma'in is flowing water, and it is the river of which God said: ﴿Your Lord has placed a stream beneath you.﴾"

* Muhammad ibn Amarah al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿a place of settlement and a flowing spring﴾, he said: "The ma'in is water."

* Muhammad ibn Amarah al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "a flowing spring" – he said: "Water."

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn as-Salt narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Salim, from Sa'id, regarding His words: ﴿a place of settlement and a flowing spring﴾, he said: "A level place, and the ma'in is visible water."

* I was told by al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard ad-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿and a flowing spring﴾: "It is visible water."

Others said: by the qarar (settlement) He means the fruits.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿a place of settlement and a flowing spring﴾, "it has fruits, and it is Bayt al-Maqdis."

* Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, the like of it.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This statement of Qatadah regarding the meaning of ﴿a place of settlement﴾, even if he did not intend by his words that it is described as "a place of settlement" only because of the fruits in it, and because of that its inhabitants settle there, has no basis that we know of. As for ﴿ma'in﴾, it is a passive participle from "ʿintuhu, fa-anā uʿīnuhu" (I assist it), and it is mu'in; it may also be a fa'il form from "ma'ana, yamʿanu," so it is ma'in from al-ma'un (abundance), and from it is the saying of Ubayd ibn al-Abras:

A broken ravine, or a flowing spring that pours forth,
or a hill, before which are crevices.

[The verse is by Ubayd ibn al-Abras from his long rhyming qasida in bāʾ (Lisan: m-ʿ-n), which the author cited at the words of God, exalted: ﴿And We sheltered them on a height, a place of settlement and a flowing spring﴾. In Lisan al-Arab it says: al-Farra said: "dhat qarar" means level land. "Ma'in al-ma'" means visible, flowing water. He said: "You may make ma'in a passive participle from al-uyun (springs), (which the author preferred), and you may make it a fa'il from al-ma'un, whose root is al-ma'n. Al-ma'in is flowing water, and it was said: flowing over the surface of the earth, and it was said: sweet and abundant, and all of that is from ease. Al-ma'n is visible water." Al-luhub is the plural of lahb (with a kasra on the lam): the gap and the air between two mountains. In al-Muhkam: "mahra" is what is between every two mountains. It was said: it is the crack in a mountain, according to al-Lihyani. It was said: it is a small ravine in a mountain. It was said: it is a face of a mountain like a wall, which cannot be climbed. End of quotation.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 23, verses 51–52:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things and act righteously. Indeed, I am Knowing of what you do.﴾ (51)

His saying, exalted is He, means: And We said to Jesus: O messengers, eat of the lawful things that God has made good for you, not the unlawful. ﴿And act righteously.﴾ One says in speech to a single man: "O people, withhold your harm from us," and as He said: ﴿Those to whom the people said﴾, and it was one man.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said in accordance with what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil related to me, saying: Ubayd ibn Ishaq al-Dabbi al-Attar related to me, from Hafs ibn Umar al-Fazari, from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from Amr ibn Shurahbil, concerning: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things and act righteously﴾, he said: Jesus son of Mary used to eat from the spinning of his mother.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am Knowing of what you do﴾

It means: Indeed, I have knowledge of your deeds; nothing of them is hidden from me, and I will recompense you for all of them and pay you your rewards and your reward for them. So take up righteous deeds and strive.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, this community of yours is one community, and I am your Lord, so fear Me.﴾ (52)

The reciters differed in the reading of His saying: ﴿And indeed, this community of yours is one community﴾. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read ﴿wa-anna﴾ with a fatha, meaning: "Indeed I am Knowing of what you do, and that this community of yours is one community." On this interpretation, ﴿anna﴾ is in the genitive position, conjoined by coordination to the ﴿ma﴾ in His saying ﴿of what you do﴾. It may also be in the accusative position if it is read thus, and the meaning of the statement would then be: "Know that this..." and its accusative would be by a hidden verb. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it with a kasra: ﴿wa-inna﴾ "this," as a resumption. In my view, the kasra on the basis of beginning is the correct reading, because the report from God about His saying to Jesus, ﴿O messengers﴾, is the subject, so His saying ﴿and indeed this﴾ is referred back to it by coordination. So the meaning of the statement is: "And We said to Jesus: O messengers, eat of the good things," and "We said: And indeed this community of yours is one community." It has been said that the word ummah (community) in this place means religion and creed.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His saying: ﴿And indeed, this community of yours is one community﴾, he said: the creed and the religion.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And I am your Lord, so fear Me﴾

It means: And I am your master, so fear Me by obeying Me, that you may be safe from My punishment. "One community" is put in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). It is related from some of them that they read it in the nominative. Some grammarians of Basra used to say: its nominative, when read as nominative, is by way of predicate, and "your community" is made accusative as an apposition (badal) to "this." As for the grammarians of Kufa, they refuse this except in poetic necessity, and they said: one does not say "I passed by this boy of yours," because "this" is followed only by the definite article and generic nouns, since "this" is an indication of a number, so there is need to specify the intended referent of the indicated thing, which of the genera it is. They said: when one says "this is your community, one community," and "the community" is absent while "this" is present, they said: it is not permissible to specify the present by the absent. They said: for that reason it is not permissible to say "indeed this Zayd is standing," because "this" requires a genus, not a proper identification.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 23, verse 53:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But they cut their affair among them into sects (zubur). Every party, in what they have, is rejoicing.﴾

The reciters differed over the reading of His saying ﴿zuburan﴾. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Iraq read ﴿zuburan﴾ as the plural of zabur (scripture). According to the reading of these reciters, the meaning of the statement is: the people whom God commanded, from the community of the Messenger Jesus, to unite upon one religion and one creed, which God commanded them to adhere to, split into ﴿zuburan﴾, meaning books. Thus each group submitted to a book other than the book which the other group submitted to, like the Jews who claimed that they followed the judgment of the Torah while they denied the judgment of the Gospel and the Qur'an, and like the Christians who submitted to the Gospel according to their claim while they denied the judgment of the Furqan (the Criterion, i.e., the Qur'an).

Mention of those who interpreted it in this way:

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿zuburan﴾, he said: books.

al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, the like of it.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿among them zuburan﴾, he said: the books of God, which they divided into pieces.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿they cut their affair among them into zuburan﴾. Mujahid said: their books, which they divided into pieces.

Others from among the people of this reading said: the meaning of the statement is: they divided their religion among them into books which they invented, arguing in them for their own doctrines.

Mention of those who said this:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿But they cut their affair among them into zuburan. Every party, in what they have, is rejoicing﴾, he said: this is what they differed over regarding religions and books; each one is pleased with his own opinion. There are no people of desires except that they are pleased with their own opinion, their desire, and their companion who fabricated that for them.

The majority of the reciters of Syria read ﴿zubaran﴾ with a damma on the zay and a fatha on the ba', meaning: they divided their affair among them into pieces, like the pieces of iron (zubar al-hadid), and each of these pieces is called zubrah, from the saying of God: ﴿Bring me blocks of iron (zubar al-hadid)﴾. So some of them became Jews, and some of them became Christians.

The reading we choose in this matter is the reading of those who read it with a damma on the zay and the ba', because the interpreters are unanimous in their interpretation that what is meant is the books. This indicates the soundness of what we have chosen, since al-zubur are the books, and it is said from it: zabartu al-kitab, when I wrote the book.

Thus the meaning of the statement is: those whom God commanded to adhere to His religion among the nations divided their religion among them into books, as we have explained before.

And His saying: ﴿Every party, in what they have, is rejoicing﴾

He says: every group of those nations, with what they have chosen for themselves of religion and books, is rejoicing, pleased with it, not seeing that the truth is other than it.

As narrated:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Every party, in what they have, is rejoicing﴾: a sect, and these are the People of the Book.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿Every party﴾: a sect of the People of the Book.

**The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 23, Verses 54–56**

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So leave them in their heedlessness for a time﴾ (54) ﴿Do they think that what We provide them with of wealth and children (55) is Us hastening to them with good things? Nay, they do not perceive (56)﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "So leave them, O Muhammad, those who have divided their affair among themselves into sects (zuburan)," ﴿in their heedlessness﴾, meaning in their misguidance and error, ﴿for a time﴾, meaning until a term that will come upon them at the arrival of My punishment.

The people of interpretation (ta'wil, the science of explaining the Qur'an) said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

- Al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿So leave them in their heedlessness for a time﴾: "In their misguidance."

- Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿So leave them in their heedlessness for a time﴾: "Al-ghamrah is al-ghamr (the flood, that which covers)."

* *

And His words: ﴿Do they think that what We provide them with of wealth and children﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Do these factions, who have divided their religion into sects, think that what We give them of worldly wealth and children ﴿is Us hastening to them﴾, meaning: We race ahead to bring them good in the good things of the Hereafter and hasten to them therein? The word "ma" in His words ﴿that We provide them with﴾ (anna-ma) is in the accusative (nasb), because it carries the meaning of alladhi (the relative pronoun "that"). ﴿Nay, they do not perceive﴾: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says, rebuking them: "That is not the case; rather, they do not know that My providing them with that wealth is only a respite and a gradual enticement toward them."

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa' told us; all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿that We provide them with﴾, he said: "We give them." ﴿We hasten to them﴾, he said: "We increase them in good, we give them respite." He said: "This is for Quraysh."

- Al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

- Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali narrated to me, he said: Ash'ath ibn Abd Allah narrated to me, he said: Shu'ba told us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', who said: I said to Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakra regarding the words of God: ﴿We hasten to them in good things﴾. He said: "He hastens to them in good things." It seems that Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakra, by his recitation (qira'ah) of it in this way, intended that its interpretation is: "He hastens to them, by Our providing them with wealth and children, in good things."

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Indeed, those who are, out of fear of their Lord, apprehensive (mushfiqun)﴾ [57] ﴿and those who believe in the signs of their Lord﴾ [58] ﴿and those who do not associate anything with their Lord﴾ [59]

He, the Exalted, means by His words: ﴿Indeed, those who are, out of fear of their Lord, apprehensive﴾, that indeed those who are apprehensive out of their fear and dread of the punishment of Allah, so they, out of that fear, are persistent in His obedience and earnest in seeking His good pleasure. ﴿And those who believe in the signs of their Lord﴾: he says, and those who affirm the signs of His Book and His proofs as true. ﴿And those who do not associate anything with their Lord﴾: he says, and those who devote their worship sincerely to their Lord, so they do not make for Him, in it, any partner for other than Him, neither an idol nor a statue, nor do they show off their worship to any of His creatures; rather, they make their deeds purely for His Face, and it is Him alone they intend with obedience and worship, to the exclusion of everything else besides Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 23, verses 60–61:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful, [knowing] that they will return to their Lord﴾ [23:60]. ﴿It is those who hasten to good deeds, and they are foremost in them﴾ [23:61].

By His saying, exalted is His remembrance, ﴿And those who give what they give﴾, He means: those who give the recipients of the zakat (sahm, the beneficiaries entitled to alms) what God has enjoined for them from their wealth. ﴿What they give﴾ means: what they give them of charity, and they render the rights of God upon them from their wealth to their rightful people. ﴿While their hearts are fearful﴾ means: fearful that they will return to their Lord, so that what they have done of that will not save them from the punishment of God. Thus they fear the return to God for that reason, as al-Hasan said: "The believer combines good works and apprehension."

Those who practise interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said concerning its interpretation.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abjar, from a man, from Ibn Umar: ﴿They give what they give while their hearts are fearful﴾ — he said: "The zakat."

- Muhammad ibn Umara narrated to me, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Israil informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid: ﴿while their hearts are fearful﴾ — he said: "The believer spends his wealth while his heart is fearful."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu al-Ashhab, from al-Hasan, who said: ﴿They give what they give while their hearts are fearful﴾ — he said: "They do the acts of righteousness they have done, and they fear that this will not save them from the punishment of their Lord."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said: ﴿They give what they give while their hearts are fearful﴾ — he said: "The believer spends his wealth and gives charity, while his heart is fearful that he is returning to his Lord."

- Yaqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, that he used to say: "The believer combines good works and apprehension, and the hypocrite combines evil deeds and security." Then al-Hasan recited: ﴿Indeed, those who are, from fear of their Lord, apprehensive﴾ up to ﴿and their hearts are fearful that they will return to their Lord﴾, and the hypocrite said: "I have been given this on knowledge that is with me."

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Yazid, from Ikrimah: ﴿They give what they give﴾ — he said: "They give what they have given." ﴿While their hearts are fearful﴾ — he says: "fearful."

- Khallad ibn Aslam narrated to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl narrated to us, saying: Israil informed us, saying: Salim al-Aftas informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His saying: ﴿And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful﴾ — he said: "They do what they do while knowing that they are heading to death, and this is among the glad tidings."

- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿They give what they give while their hearts are fearful﴾ — he said: "They give what they have been given and do what they have done of good, while their hearts are fearful."

- al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, the like of it.

- Ali narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: ﴿those who come with what they came with while their hearts are fearful﴾ — he says: "They act while fearing."

- He said: Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: ﴿And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful﴾ — he said: "They give what they have given, out of awe of God and fear of God."

- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His saying: ﴿They give what they give﴾ — "They spend what they have spent."

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿They give what they give while their hearts are fearful﴾ — he said: "They give what they have given, spend what they have spent, and give charity with what they have given in charity, while their hearts are fearful, guarding against the wrath of God and the Fire."

Upon this reading, namely ﴿And those who give what they give﴾, is the reading of the regional readers (qurra' al-amsar), and it is in the script of their codices, and by it we recite; because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it, and its agreement with the script of the codices of the Muslims.

And it is related from Aisha, may God be pleased with her, concerning that:

- Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Thabit narrated to us, from Talhah ibn Amr, from Abu Khalaf, who said: I entered with Ubayd ibn Umayr upon Aisha, and Ubayd asked her: "How do we recite this letter: ﴿And those who give what they give﴾?" She said: "﴿Those who come with what they came with﴾." It seems she interpreted it as: "those who do what they do of good deeds while fearing God."

Like what:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated to us, saying: Umar ibn Qays narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'id ibn Wahb al-Hamdani, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Aisha said: "O Messenger of God, ﴿And those who come with what they came with while their hearts are fearful﴾ — is it the one who commits a sin while fearing it?" He said: "No, but rather the one who fasts, prays, and gives charity while fearing."

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Malik ibn Mighwal, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'id ibn Wahb, that Aisha said: "I said: O Messenger of God, ﴿Those who come with what they came with while their hearts are fearful﴾ — are they those who sin while being apprehensive? And fast while being apprehensive?" [[Possibly there is a lacuna here; the original is: He said: "No, but rather those who pray while being apprehensive, and fast..." etc., as is clear from the hadith of Aisha that follows.]] Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Layth narrated to us, from Mughith, from a man of Makkah, from Aisha, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, ﴿Those who come with what they came with while their hearts are fearful﴾ — he said: and mentioned the like of this.

- Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Malik ibn Mighwal, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'id, that Aisha said: "O Messenger of God, ﴿Those who come with what they came with while their hearts are fearful﴾ — is it the man who commits adultery, steals, and drinks wine?" He said: "No, O daughter of Abu Bakr, or O daughter of the Siddiq, but rather it is the man who fasts, prays, gives charity, and fears that it will not be accepted from him."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to me, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, and Hushaym from al-Awwam ibn Hawshab, both from Aisha, who said: I asked the Messenger of God ﷺ, and he said: "O daughter of Abu Bakr, or O daughter of the Siddiq, they are those who pray and fear that it will not be accepted from them."

And that the phrase ﴿that they will return to their Lord﴾ is in the accusative position, because the meaning of the statement is: ﴿and their hearts are fearful﴾ of that they will return. So when the preposition ﴿min﴾ was omitted, the preceding statement connected to it and it took the accusative. Some of them said it is in the genitive position, even though the governing particle is not apparent.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿It is those who hasten to good deeds﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: those whose attributes are these attributes hasten in righteous deeds and seek nearness to God through obedience to Him.

As:

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿It is those who hasten to good deeds﴾.

He said: "The good deeds are: fear, apprehension, faith, and restraint from associating partners with God; that is the racing to these good deeds."

* *

His saying: ﴿And they are foremost in them﴾

Some of them said: its meaning is that happiness had preceded for them from God, and that is their foremostness in the good deeds they do.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: ﴿And they are foremost in them﴾ — he says: "Happiness preceded for them."

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿And they are foremost in them﴾: "Those are the good deeds."

Some interpreted it to mean: "and they are toward them foremost," and others interpreted it to mean: "and they are foremost because of them."

The most correct of these sayings in my view is the saying of Ibn Abbas, that happiness had preceded for them from God before their hastening in good deeds, and because of what had preceded for them of that, they hastened in them.

I only said that this is the more preferable of the two interpretations of the statement because it is the more apparent of its two meanings, and because we have no need, when we orient the interpretation of the statement this way, to shift the meaning of the particle "la-" in His saying ﴿lahā sābiqūn﴾ away from its more prevalent meaning.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 23, verses 62–63:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity, and with Us is a Record which speaks with truth, and they will not be wronged.﴾ (62)

He, the Exalted, says: We do not burden a soul except with what is within its capacity and suitable for it in worship; for this reason We imposed upon it what We imposed, namely knowledge of the oneness of God, and We legislated for it what We legislated of the laws.

﴿And with Us is a Record which speaks with truth﴾ means: with Us is the book of the deeds of creatures, of what they did of good and evil, which speaks with truth. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾ means: it clearly states, with truthfulness, what they did of deeds in the world, with neither addition nor deficiency; and We will fully repay all of them their rewards, the good-doer for his goodness and the evildoer for his evil. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾ means: they will not be wronged by having added to the evil deeds of the evildoer among them what he did not do, so that he is punished for other than his offence, nor by diminishing the good-doer from what he did of goodness, so that his reward is reduced.

* *

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Nay, their hearts are in confusion about this, and they have deeds other than that which they are doing.﴾ (63)

He, the Exalted, says: The matter is not as these polytheists suppose, that Our giving them wealth and children is a good We are hastening to them and a sign of Our approval of them; rather, their hearts are in a state of confusion, blindness regarding this Qur'an. By "ghamra" (confusion) he means that which covers their hearts and conceals them from understanding the admonitions, lessons and proofs which God placed in His Book. By His saying ﴿about this﴾ he means the Qur'an.

The people of interpretation have said what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, who said: Abu Asim related to us, who said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿in confusion about this﴾: he said: in blindness regarding this Qur'an.

- al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿in confusion about this﴾: he said: from the Qur'an.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and they have deeds other than that which they are doing﴾

He, the Exalted, says: these disbelievers have deeds, of sins, which God does not approve. ﴿Other than that﴾ means: other than the deeds of the people of faith in God and of those who are mindful of Him and fear Him.

The people of interpretation have said what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Hakkam related to us, from Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid: ﴿and they have deeds other than that﴾ he said: sins.

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, who said: Abu Asim related to us, who said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and they have deeds other than that﴾: he said: the truth.

- Ali ibn Sahl related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and they have deeds other than that﴾: he said: sins other than that truth.

- Hajjaj related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliya, regarding His saying ﴿and they have deeds other than that﴾ ... the verse, he said: deeds other than the truth.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 23, verses 62–63:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity, and with Us is a Record which speaks with truth, and they will not be wronged.﴾ (62)

He, the Exalted, says: We do not burden a soul except with what is within its capacity and suitable for it in worship; for this reason We imposed upon it what We imposed, namely knowledge of the oneness of God, and We legislated for it what We legislated of the laws.

﴿And with Us is a Record which speaks with truth﴾ means: with Us is the book of the deeds of creatures, of what they did of good and evil, which speaks with truth. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾ means: it clearly states, with truthfulness, what they did of deeds in the world, with neither addition nor deficiency; and We will fully repay all of them their rewards, the good-doer for his goodness and the evildoer for his evil. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾ means: they will not be wronged by having added to the evil deeds of the evildoer among them what he did not do, so that he is punished for other than his offence, nor by diminishing the good-doer from what he did of goodness, so that his reward is reduced.

* *

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Nay, their hearts are in confusion about this, and they have deeds other than that which they are doing.﴾ (63)

He, the Exalted, says: The matter is not as these polytheists suppose, that Our giving them wealth and children is a good We are hastening to them and a sign of Our approval of them; rather, their hearts are in a state of confusion, blindness regarding this Qur'an. By "ghamra" (confusion) he means that which covers their hearts and conceals them from understanding the admonitions, lessons and proofs which God placed in His Book. By His saying ﴿about this﴾ he means the Qur'an.

The people of interpretation have said what we have said on this.

- al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿in confusion about this﴾: he said: from the Qur'an.

* *

He, the Exalted, says: these disbelievers have deeds, of sins, which God does not approve. ﴿Other than that﴾ means: other than the deeds of the people of faith in God and of those who are mindful of Him and fear Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 23, verses 64–65:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Until, when We seize their affluent ones with the punishment, behold, they cry out for help.﴾ (64) ﴿Do not cry out for help today; indeed, you will not be given help from Us.﴾ (65)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: For these disbelievers of Quraysh there are deeds other than that which they are doing, until the people of luxury and insolence among them are seized with the punishment. As follows:

⁕ Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding ﴿when We seize their affluent ones with the punishment﴾: "The mutrafun (affluent ones) are the great ones [al-'uzama']." ﴿Behold, they cry out for help﴾: He says: when We seize them with it, they cry out, meaning they wail and call for help because of what has befallen them of Our punishment. The ju'ar (crying out) is raising the voice, as a bull bellows (yaje'ar al-thawr). And from it is the saying of al-A'sha:

"He alternates between the prayers of the king, at times prostrating and at times crying out (ju'ara)..."

[The verse is by al-A'sha (his Diwan, Cairo edition with the commentary of Dr. Muhammad Husayn, p. 53), and it is from a qasida in which al-A'sha praises Qays ibn Ma'd Yakrib. "Yuraawih bayn al-'alamayn" means he alternates between these two matters, one at one time and the other at another. Al-ju'ar is the verbal noun of ja'ara ila Allah: when one humbles himself and raises his voice. He says: the one he praises, along with what he is described with of generosity, strength and fidelity, is pious, watching over his Lord, humbling himself to Him and crying out in his prayers. The author cited it as evidence that al-ju'ar is raising the voice, as a bull bellows.]

Scholars of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

⁕ Ali narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿behold, they cry out for help﴾ means: they seek help (yastaghithun).

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya and Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Alqama ibn Qardad, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Until, when We seize their affluent ones with the punishment, behold, they cry out for help﴾, he said: "With swords, on the day of Badr."

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding His saying: ﴿behold, they cry out for help﴾, he said: "They become distressed (yajza'un)."

⁕ He said: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿Until, when We seize their affluent ones with the punishment﴾, he said: "The punishment of the day of Badr." ﴿Behold, they cry out for help﴾, he said: "Those who are in Makkah."

⁕ I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿Until, when We seize their affluent ones with the punishment﴾, meaning the people of Badr, Allah seized them with the punishment on the day of Badr.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Ibn Zayd say regarding His saying: ﴿behold, they cry out for help﴾, he said: "They become distressed (yajza'un)."

* *

And His saying: ﴿Do not cry out for help today﴾

He says: Do not wail and seek help today, when the punishment that is not averted from those who wronged themselves has descended upon you. Indeed, your wailing will not benefit you, nor will it ward off from you anything of the wrath of Allah that has already descended upon you. ﴿Indeed, you will not be given help from Us﴾: He says: Indeed, you will not be rescued from Our punishment that has descended upon you, and nothing will deliver you from it.

Scholars of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said in interpreting this.

Those who said this:

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas: ﴿Do not cry out for help today﴾: "Do not become distressed today."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: al-Rabi' ibn Anas informed us: ﴿Do not cry out for help today﴾: "Do not become distressed now, when the punishment has descended upon you; indeed, it will not benefit you. Had this distress been before, it would have benefited you."

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed My verses were recited to you, but you turned back on your heels, retreating (66), arrogant concerning it, conversing by night, speaking nonsense (67)﴾

Says He, exalted is His remembrance, to these polytheists of Quraysh: Do not cry out today, when the wrath and punishment of Allah have descended upon you, for what your hands have earned and what you have deserved by your disbelief in the signs of your Lord. ﴿Indeed My verses were recited to you﴾ meaning: the verses of the Book of Allah. He says: My verses of Scripture were recited to you, and you denied them and turned away, retreating from them when you heard them, out of your aversion to hearing them. And thus it is said of everyone who returns the way he came: "So-and-so turned back on his heels" (nakasa 'ala 'aqibihi).

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what is similar to what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿but you turned back on your heels, retreating﴾, he said: you draw back.

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿so you turned back on your heels, retreating﴾, he says: you reflect (tudabbirun).

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed My verses were recited to you, but you turned back on your heels, retreating﴾, he means the people of Mecca.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿retreating﴾, he said: you draw back.

* *

And His saying: ﴿arrogant concerning it﴾

He says: arrogant regarding the sanctuary of Allah, saying: no one will prevail over us in it, for we are the People of the Sanctuary (ahl al-haram).

And the people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said regarding the interpretation of that.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿arrogant concerning it﴾, he says: arrogant regarding the sanctity of the House, [claiming] that no one will prevail over us in it.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿arrogant concerning it﴾, he said: in Mecca, the city.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdha narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan: (arrogant concerning it), he said: arrogant regarding my sanctuary.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying: ﴿arrogant concerning it﴾: in the sanctuary.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿arrogant concerning it﴾, he said: arrogant regarding the sanctuary.

al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, the same.

It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿arrogant concerning it﴾: in the sanctuary.

* *

And His saying: ﴿conversing by night﴾

He means: you converse (tasmurun) by night. He used the singular ﴿samiran﴾ while it carries the meaning of the plural (summar), because it was placed in the position of a time expression. The meaning of the statement is: and you speak nonsense at night, so ﴿samir﴾ was placed in the position of "night," and therefore it is in the singular. Some Basran grammarians said: it is singular in form but its meaning is plural, as one says "tifl" (a child) in place of "atfal" (children). What clarifies the correctness of what we have said, that it was placed in the position of a time expression and therefore is singular, is the poet's verse:

"Min dunihim in ji'tahum samaran ... 'azfu l-qiyani wa majlisun ghamru"

He said "samaran" because its meaning is: if you come to them at night while they are conversing (yasmurun). Likewise His saying: ﴿samiran﴾.

And the people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said concerning that.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿samiran﴾, he says: they converse around the House.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿samiran﴾, he said: a gathering at night.

al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿samiran﴾, he said: gatherings.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿samiran﴾, he said: you converse at night.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿samiran﴾: they used to converse all night and play, speaking in poetry, soothsaying, and about things they did not know.

It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿samiran﴾: he means the night conversation.

And some of them said regarding that:

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿samiran﴾, he says: a converser from the people of the sanctuary, safe and unafraid, they used to say: we are the People of the Sanctuary, we do not fear.

al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿samiran﴾, he says: a converser from the people of Mecca, safe and unafraid; he said: they used to say: we are the People of the Sanctuary, we do not fear.

* *

And His saying: ﴿tahjurun﴾

The reciters differed regarding its recitation. The common reciters of the major cities recited it: ﴿tahjurun﴾ with a fatha on the ta and a damma on the jim. There are two meanings for the reading of those who read it thus: one is that it means He described them as turning away from the Qur'an, or the House, or the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and abandoning him. The other is that it means they say some speech as a man speaks in his sleep, which is when he raves; so it is as if He described them as saying in the Qur'an what has no meaning, namely that they say falsehood about it which does no harm. Both interpretations have come from the people of interpretation.

Mention of those who said: they were turning away from the remembrance of Allah and the truth and abandoning it:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿tahjurun﴾, he said: they abandon the remembrance of Allah and the truth.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Samad narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying: ﴿samiran tahjurun﴾, he said: cursing.

Mention of those who said: they were saying falsehood and evil speech regarding the Qur'an:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿tahjurun﴾, he said: they speak nonsense in falsehood.

He said: Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Hubayr: ﴿samiran tahjurun﴾, he said: they converse at night, plunging into falsehood.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿tahjurun﴾, he said: with evil speech regarding the Qur'an.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿tahjurun﴾, he said: al-hadhayan (raving), speaking what one does not intend and does not understand, like the sick man who speaks what he does not know. He said: Ubayy used to recite it: ﴿samiran tahjurun﴾.

Others recited it: ﴿samiran tuhjirun﴾ with a damma on the ta and a kasra on the jim. Among the common reciters of the major cities who read it thus was Nafi ibn Abi Nu'aym, meaning: they use obscene language in speech and utter abuse, from the saying "ahjara al-rajul" (the man uttered obscenity) when he spoke foully. It is mentioned that they used to revile the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Mention of those who said that:

Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿tuhjirun﴾, he said: you say hujr (obscenity).

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Mu'min narrated to us, from Abu Nuhayk, from Ikrima, that he recited: ﴿samiran tahjurun﴾: meaning, they revile.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdha narrated to us, saying: Awn narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿samiran tuhjirun﴾: my messenger.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, who said: al-Hasan said: ﴿tuhjirun﴾: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿tuhjirun﴾, he says: they say evil.

al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: al-Hasan said: ﴿tuhjirun﴾: the Book of Allah and His Messenger.

It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿tuhjirun﴾: he says: they say the reprehensible and obscene speech; thus hujr is speech.

And the reading that is most correct in our view is the reading upon which the common reciters of the major cities agree, namely the fatha on the ta and the damma on the jim, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters.

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed My verses were recited to you, but you turned back on your heels, retreating (66), arrogant concerning it, conversing by night, speaking nonsense (67)﴾

Says He, exalted is His remembrance, to these polytheists of Quraysh: Do not cry out today, when the wrath and punishment of Allah have descended upon you, for what your hands have earned and what you have deserved by your disbelief in the signs of your Lord. ﴿Indeed My verses were recited to you﴾ meaning: the verses of the Book of Allah. He says: My verses of Scripture were recited to you, and you denied them and turned away, retreating from them when you heard them, out of your aversion to hearing them. And thus it is said of everyone who returns the way he came: "So-and-so turned back on his heels" (nakasa 'ala 'aqibihi).

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what is similar to what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿but you turned back on your heels, retreating﴾, he said: you draw back.

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿so you turned back on your heels, retreating﴾, he says: you reflect (tudabbirun).

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed My verses were recited to you, but you turned back on your heels, retreating﴾, he means the people of Mecca.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿retreating﴾, he said: you draw back.

* *

And His saying: ﴿arrogant concerning it﴾

He says: arrogant regarding the sanctuary of Allah, saying: no one will prevail over us in it, for we are the People of the Sanctuary (ahl al-haram).

And the people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said regarding the interpretation of that.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿arrogant concerning it﴾, he says: arrogant regarding the sanctity of the House, [claiming] that no one will prevail over us in it.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿arrogant concerning it﴾, he said: in Mecca, the city.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdha narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan: (arrogant concerning it), he said: arrogant regarding my sanctuary.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying: ﴿arrogant concerning it﴾: in the sanctuary.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿arrogant concerning it﴾, he said: arrogant regarding the sanctuary.

al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, the same.

It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿arrogant concerning it﴾: in the sanctuary.

* *

And His saying: ﴿conversing by night﴾

He means: you converse (tasmurun) by night. He used the singular ﴿samiran﴾ while it carries the meaning of the plural (summar), because it was placed in the position of a time expression. The meaning of the statement is: and you speak nonsense at night, so ﴿samir﴾ was placed in the position of "night," and therefore it is in the singular. Some Basran grammarians said: it is singular in form but its meaning is plural, as one says "tifl" (a child) in place of "atfal" (children). What clarifies the correctness of what we have said, that it was placed in the position of a time expression and therefore is singular, is the poet's verse:

"Min dunihim in ji'tahum samaran ... 'azfu l-qiyani wa majlisun ghamru"

He said "samaran" because its meaning is: if you come to them at night while they are conversing (yasmurun). Likewise His saying: ﴿samiran﴾.

And the people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said concerning that.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿samiran﴾, he says: they converse around the House.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿samiran﴾, he said: a gathering at night.

al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿samiran﴾, he said: gatherings.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿samiran﴾, he said: you converse at night.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿samiran﴾: they used to converse all night and play, speaking in poetry, soothsaying, and about things they did not know.

It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿samiran﴾: he means the night conversation.

And some of them said regarding that:

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿samiran﴾, he says: a converser from the people of the sanctuary, safe and unafraid, they used to say: we are the People of the Sanctuary, we do not fear.

al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿samiran﴾, he says: a converser from the people of Mecca, safe and unafraid; he said: they used to say: we are the People of the Sanctuary, we do not fear.

* *

And His saying: ﴿tahjurun﴾

The reciters differed regarding its recitation. The common reciters of the major cities recited it: ﴿tahjurun﴾ with a fatha on the ta and a damma on the jim. There are two meanings for the reading of those who read it thus: one is that it means He described them as turning away from the Qur'an, or the House, or the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and abandoning him. The other is that it means they say some speech as a man speaks in his sleep, which is when he raves; so it is as if He described them as saying in the Qur'an what has no meaning, namely that they say falsehood about it which does no harm. Both interpretations have come from the people of interpretation.

Mention of those who said: they were turning away from the remembrance of Allah and the truth and abandoning it:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿tahjurun﴾, he said: they abandon the remembrance of Allah and the truth.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Samad narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying: ﴿samiran tahjurun﴾, he said: cursing.

Mention of those who said: they were saying falsehood and evil speech regarding the Qur'an:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿tahjurun﴾, he said: they speak nonsense in falsehood.

He said: Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Hubayr: ﴿samiran tahjurun﴾, he said: they converse at night, plunging into falsehood.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿tahjurun﴾, he said: with evil speech regarding the Qur'an.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿tahjurun﴾, he said: al-hadhayan (raving), speaking what one does not intend and does not understand, like the sick man who speaks what he does not know. He said: Ubayy used to recite it: ﴿samiran tahjurun﴾.

Others recited it: ﴿samiran tuhjirun﴾ with a damma on the ta and a kasra on the jim. Among the common reciters of the major cities who read it thus was Nafi ibn Abi Nu'aym, meaning: they use obscene language in speech and utter abuse, from the saying "ahjara al-rajul" (the man uttered obscenity) when he spoke foully. It is mentioned that they used to revile the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Mention of those who said that:

Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿tuhjirun﴾, he said: you say hujr (obscenity).

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Mu'min narrated to us, from Abu Nuhayk, from Ikrima, that he recited: ﴿samiran tahjurun﴾: meaning, they revile.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdha narrated to us, saying: Awn narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿samiran tuhjirun﴾: my messenger.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, who said: al-Hasan said: ﴿tuhjirun﴾: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿tuhjirun﴾, he says: they say evil.

al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: al-Hasan said: ﴿tuhjirun﴾: the Book of Allah and His Messenger.

It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿tuhjirun﴾: he says: they say the reprehensible and obscene speech; thus hujr is speech.

And the reading that is most correct in our view is the reading upon which the common reciters of the major cities agree, namely the fatha on the ta and the damma on the jim, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 23, verse 68–70:

The explanation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not then pondered over the Word, or has there come to them that which did not come to their forefathers of old?﴾ (68) ﴿Or did they not know their Messenger, so that they deny him?﴾ (69) ﴿Or do they say, "He has madness in him"? Nay, he has brought them the truth, but most of them are averse to the truth.﴾ (70)

His Lord, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Have these polytheists not pondered over the revelation of Allah and His speech, so that they would know the lessons contained in it and recognize the proofs of Allah with which He argued against them in it? ﴿Or has there come to them that which did not come to their forefathers of old?﴾ He says: Or has there come to them a matter that did not come to their predecessors, their ancestors, so that they reject it with disdain and turn away? For messengers came before them, and Books were sent down along with them. It is also possible that "am" (or) in this place means "bal" (rather), so the meaning of the speech would be: Have they not pondered over the Word? Rather, there has come to them what did not come to their forefathers of old, so they abandoned that reflection and turned away from it, since nothing like it had been among their ancestors who preceded them. This has been reported from Ibn Abbas regarding a similar statement.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Have they not then pondered over the Word, or has there come to them that which did not come to their forefathers of old?﴾ He said: "By my life, there has indeed come to them what did not come to their forefathers of old, but [the sense is]: Or has there not come to them what did not come to their forefathers of old?"

* *

And His words: ﴿Or did they not know their Messenger, so that they deny him?﴾

His Lord, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Or did these deniers not know Muhammad, and that he is of the people of truthfulness and trustworthiness, so that they deny him? That is, so that they reject his speech, or they did not know him as truthful, and argue that they do not know him. His Lord, majestic is His praise, says: How then do they deny him while they know him among them as truthful and trustworthy? ﴿Or do they say, "He has madness in him"?﴾ That is: Do they say that Muhammad has madness, so that he speaks what has no meaning, does not understand, and does not know what he is saying? ﴿Nay, he has brought them the truth﴾

His Lord, may His remembrance be exalted, says: If they say that, then their lie in that saying is clear and evident, because a madman raves and utters speech that has no meaning, and he does not reason or understand. What Muhammad brought them is the wisdom beyond which there is no greater wisdom, and the truth whose soundness is not hidden from one of sound nature. So how could it be said that it is the speech of a madman?

* *

And His words: ﴿But most of them are averse to the truth.﴾

His Lord, may His remembrance be exalted, says: These unbelievers do not fail to know Muhammad as truthful, nor is it that Muhammad is regarded by them as a madman. Rather, they have known him to be truthful and right in what he says and in what he calls them to. But most of them are unwilling to submit to the truth and are displeased with following Muhammad, out of envy toward him, animosity against him, and arrogance on the earth.
