Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 23, verse 71:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted. Rather, We have brought them their reminder, but they, from their reminder, are turning away.﴾ (23:71)

The Exalted, may His remembrance be exalted, says: If the Lord, may His remembrance be exalted, had acted according to what these polytheists desire, and had made the governance follow their will and wish, and abandoned the truth which they dislike, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted. That is because they do not know the outcomes of affairs, nor what is sound and what is corrupt in governance. So if affairs were running according to their will and desires, with most of them preferring falsehood over truth, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them of God's creation would not have remained, because they stand by the truth.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of exegesis) have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: al-Suddi narrated to us, from Abu Salih, regarding ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires﴾: he said: "God."

* He said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires﴾: he said: "The truth: it is God."

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding his saying: ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires﴾: he said: "The truth: God."

* * *

And His saying: ﴿Rather, We have brought them their reminder, but they, from their reminder, are turning away.﴾

The scholars of exegesis differed regarding the interpretation of "reminder" (dhikr) in this place. Some of them said: it is the clarification of the truth for them by what was sent down to a man among them from this Qur'an.

Mention of those who said that:

* 'Ali narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding his saying: ﴿Rather, We have brought them their reminder﴾: he means: "We made it clear to them."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "Rather, We have brought them their honour (sharaf)"; this Qur'an was an honour for them, since it was sent down to a man from among them, but they turned away from it and disbelieved in it. They said: this is similar to His saying: ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and for your people﴾ (43:44). These two statements are close in meaning, because God, may His praise be exalted, sent down this Qur'an as a clarification, explaining what His creatures need regarding the matters of their religion, and it is also a reminder for His Messenger (ﷺ) and his people and an honour for them.

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Or do you ask them for any payment? But the payment of your Lord is better, and He is the best of providers (72). And indeed, you invite them to a straight path (73).﴾

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be exalted: Or do you ask these polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, for a payment (kharaj), meaning a wage for what you have brought them from Allah of counsel and truth? ﴿But the payment of your Lord is better﴾: the wage of your Lord for your carrying out His command and seeking His good pleasure is better for you than that. The Prophet ﷺ did not ask them for any wage for what Allah brought them; he said to them what Allah said to him, and He commanded him to say it to them: ﴿Say, "I do not ask you for it any wage, except affection among relatives"﴾. The meaning of the speech is: Do you ask them for a wage for what you have brought them, so that they turn back on their heels when you recite it to them, arrogant in the sacred precinct? Then the payment of your Lord is better.

And those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿Or do you ask them for any payment? But the payment of your Lord is better﴾, he said: "A wage."

al-Hasan related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq related to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan, the like of it.

The root of al-kharaj and al-kharj are two verbal nouns that are not used in the plural.

* *

His words: ﴿and He is the best of providers﴾

He says: And Allah is the best of those who give a reward for a deed, and the best of those who grant provision.

* *

His words: ﴿And indeed, you invite them to a straight path﴾

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be exalted: And indeed you, O Muhammad, invite these polytheists of your people to the religion of Islam, which is the direct road and the straight path in which there is no crookedness.

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Or do you ask them for any payment? But the payment of your Lord is better, and He is the best of providers (72). And indeed, you invite them to a straight path (73).﴾

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be exalted: Or do you ask these polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, for a payment (kharaj), meaning a wage for what you have brought them from Allah of counsel and truth? ﴿But the payment of your Lord is better﴾: the wage of your Lord for your carrying out His command and seeking His good pleasure is better for you than that. The Prophet ﷺ did not ask them for any wage for what Allah brought them; he said to them what Allah said to him, and He commanded him to say it to them: ﴿Say, "I do not ask you for it any wage, except affection among relatives"﴾. The meaning of the speech is: Do you ask them for a wage for what you have brought them, so that they turn back on their heels when you recite it to them, arrogant in the sacred precinct? Then the payment of your Lord is better.

And those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿Or do you ask them for any payment? But the payment of your Lord is better﴾, he said: "A wage."

al-Hasan related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq related to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan, the like of it.

The root of al-kharaj and al-kharj are two verbal nouns that are not used in the plural.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 23, verses 74–76:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are deviating from the path (al-sirat), ﴾ [23:74] ﴿And even if We had mercy upon them and removed what afflicts them of adversity, they would persist in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾ [23:75]

He, the Exalted, says: Those who do not affirm the resurrection after death, the rising of the Hour, and God's recompense of His servants in the Hereafter, ﴿are deviating from the path﴾ means: they turn away from the highway of truth and the straight way, and that is the religion of God which He has approved for His servants, the just. It is said of this: "So-and-so has deviated (nakaba) from such-and-such," when he swerves away from it; and "he deviated from it," meaning he turned away from it.

Interpreters have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿deviating from the path﴾, he said: "those who swerve."

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are deviating from the path﴾, he said: "they swerve from the truth."

* *

And His saying: ﴿And even if We had mercy upon them and removed what afflicts them of adversity﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Even if We had shown mercy to these who do not believe in the Hereafter, and lifted from them what afflicts them of famine, drought, and the harm of hunger and emaciation; ﴿they would persist in their transgression﴾ means: in their insolence and their boldness against their Lord. ﴿wandering blindly﴾ means: hesitating and vacillating.

As:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: ﴿And even if We had mercy upon them and removed what afflicts them of adversity﴾, he said: "hunger."

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And We had already seized them with punishment, yet they did not humble themselves before their Lord, nor did they supplicate﴾ [23:76]

He, the Exalted, says: We had already seized these polytheists with Our punishment, sent down upon them Our might, and visited Our wrath upon them, straitened their livelihoods, made their lands barren, and slain their chieftains with the sword. ﴿Yet they did not humble themselves before their Lord﴾ means: they did not submit to their Lord so as to comply with His command and prohibition, and turn in repentance to His obedience; ﴿nor did they supplicate﴾ means: nor did they abase themselves before Him.

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God ﷺ when God seized the Quraysh with years of drought, when the Messenger of God ﷺ invoked against them.

Report on that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumayla narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Yazid, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Sufyan came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, I adjure you by God and by kinship! We have eaten the 'ilhiz!" meaning the fur and blood. So God revealed: ﴿And We had already seized them with punishment, yet they did not humble themselves before their Lord, nor did they supplicate﴾.

Then Abu Sufyan came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Do you not claim that you were sent as a mercy to the worlds?" He said: "Yes!" He said: "You have slain the fathers with the sword and the sons with hunger!" So God revealed: ﴿And We had already seized them with punishment...﴾ the verse.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated to us, saying: Amr informed us, saying: al-Hasan said: "When people are afflicted by a trial from Satan, it is only a vengeance. The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 23, verse 77:

The interpretation (ta'wil) of this verse: the exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning its meaning. Some of them said: its meaning is, "until when We open upon them the gate of battle, and they are slain on the day of Badr."

Those who said this:

- Ishaq ibn Shahin related to me, saying: Khalid ibn Abdullah told us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿until when We open upon them a gate of severe punishment﴾. It has passed: it was the day of Badr.

- Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Abd al-A'la told me, saying: Dawud told us, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.

- al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿until when We open upon them a gate of severe punishment﴾. He said: the day of Badr.

Others said: its meaning is, "until when We open upon them the gate of famine and hardship, and it is the gate of severe punishment."

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his words: ﴿until when We open upon them a gate of severe punishment﴾. He said: for the disbelievers of Quraysh, the famine; and the narrative before it was also concerning them.

- al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similar to it, except that he said: "and what came before it also."

This saying which Mujahid stated is more fitting as the interpretation of the verse, because of the soundness of the report we mentioned earlier from Ibn Abbas, that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning the famine which afflicted Quraysh, by the supplication of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) against them, and the command of Thumamah ibn Uthal. And that, without doubt, was after the battle of Badr.

* *

As for His words: ﴿behold, they will be plunged into despair therein﴾:

He says: behold, these polytheists, in what We have opened upon them of punishment, are grieved and remorseful over what preceded from them, in their denial of the signs of Allah, at a time when remorse and grief will not benefit them.

**Commentary on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And it is He who produced for you hearing and sight and hearts; little are you grateful﴾ (78)**

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: And God, who brought into being for you, O deniers of the Resurrection after death, the hearing with which you hear, the sights with which you see, and the hearts (afʾidah) with which you understand. So how can it be difficult for the One who originated these things to restore them after their non-existence and loss, when He is the One who brings all of that into being whenever He wills and annihilates it whenever He desires? ﴿little are you grateful﴾ means: you, O deniers, give thanks for God's bounty in His gifts of hearing, sight and hearts only a little.

* *

**Commentary on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And it is He who multiplied you upon the earth, and to Him you will be gathered﴾ (79)**

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: And God is the One who created you on the earth, and to Him you will be gathered after your death, then you will be raised from your graves to the place of reckoning.

* *

**Commentary on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And it is He who gives life and causes death, and His is the alternation of the night and the day; will you not then reason?﴾ (80)**

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: And God is the One who gives life to His creatures, meaning He makes them living after they were lifeless drops of semen (nutfan amwatan), by breathing the spirit into them after the stages (al-tarat) that pass over them. ﴿and causes death﴾ means: and He causes them to die after He has given them life. ﴿and His is the alternation of the night and the day﴾ means: and it is He who made the night and the day alternate, just as it is said in speech, "To you is the favor and the bounty," meaning: you are the one who bestows favor and bounty.

* *

As for His words: ﴿will you not then reason?﴾

It means: will you not reason, O people, that the One who did these deeds originating them without a prior root is not incapable of reviving the dead after their perishing, and of producing again what He has willed to annihilate after producing it?

* *

**Commentary on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Nay, but they said the like of what the ancients said. They said: "When we are dead and have become dust and bones, shall we indeed be raised up?"﴾ (81–82)**

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: These polytheists have not taken heed from the signs of God, nor have they contemplated the proofs that were presented to them, demonstrating His power to do whatever He wills. Rather, they said the like of what their predecessors from the nations that denied their messengers before them had said: ﴿They said: "When we are dead and have become dust and bones"﴾ means: when we die and become dust, our bodies having decayed and our bones separated from our flesh, ﴿shall we indeed be raised up?﴾ means: shall we indeed be raised up from our graves alive, in the same state we were in before death? Verily, this is a thing that will not come to pass.

**Commentary on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And it is He who produced for you hearing and sight and hearts; little are you grateful﴾ (78)**

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: And God, who brought into being for you, O deniers of the Resurrection after death, the hearing with which you hear, the sights with which you see, and the hearts (afʾidah) with which you understand. So how can it be difficult for the One who originated these things to restore them after their non-existence and loss, when He is the One who brings all of that into being whenever He wills and annihilates it whenever He desires? ﴿little are you grateful﴾ means: you, O deniers, give thanks for God's bounty in His gifts of hearing, sight and hearts only a little.

* *

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: And God is the One who created you on the earth, and to Him you will be gathered after your death, then you will be raised from your graves to the place of reckoning.

* *

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: And God is the One who gives life to His creatures, meaning He makes them living after they were lifeless drops of semen (nutfan amwatan), by breathing the spirit into them after the stages (al-tarat) that pass over them. ﴿and causes death﴾ means: and He causes them to die after He has given them life. ﴿and His is the alternation of the night and the day﴾ means: and it is He who made the night and the day alternate, just as it is said in speech, "To you is the favor and the bounty," meaning: you are the one who bestows favor and bounty.

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it, if you know?" They will say, "To God." Say, "Will you not then remember?"﴾ (23:84–85)**

Then He informs him that they will acknowledge that it belongs to God as its sole possessor, to the exclusion of all other things besides Him. ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾ means: so say to them, when they answer you with that, "Will you not then remember?", so that you may know that whoever is able to create that from the beginning is able to bring them back to life after their death and to restore them as a sound creation after their annihilation.

* *

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne?" They will say, "To God." Say, "Will you not then fear Him?"﴾ (23:86–87)**

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say to them, O Muhammad: Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Throne that encompasses all of that? They will say: all of that belongs to God, and He is their Lord. So say to them: Will you not then fear His punishment for your disbelief in Him and your denial of His report and the report of His Messenger?

The readers (qurra') have differed regarding the recitation of His words ﴿They will say, "To God"﴾. The majority of the readers of Hijaz, Iraq and Sham recited it as ﴿sayaqūlūna lillāh﴾, except Abu 'Amr, who differed from them and recited it in this place as "sayaqūlūna Allāh" (without the lām), and in the next instance following it, in conformity with the script of the mushaf (the codified written copy of the Qur'an) — for that is how it is written in the mushafs of the cities — except in the mushaf of the people of Basra, where both instances are written with an alif. So they recited both with the alif, in conformity with the script of their mushaf. As for those who recited it with the alif, there is no difficulty in their recitation, because they treated the answer as a nominal sentence (beginning) and matched a nominative with a nominative. The meaning of the speech according to their recitation is: "Say: Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne? They will say: the Lord of that is God." So there is no difficulty in reciting it in this way. As for those who recited it without the alif in this instance and the one following it, they said: the meaning of His words "Say: Who is the Lord of the heavens?" is "To whom belong the heavens? To whom does the dominion of that belong?" So the answer was given in terms of meaning, and it was said "To God", because the question concerns to whom the dominion of that belongs. They said: this is like the saying of someone to a man: "Who is your master?", and the one answering responds to the meaning of what was asked, saying: "I belong to so-and-so", because what is understood from the answer is the same as what is understood from saying: "My master is so-and-so."

Some of them mentioned that a man of the Banu 'Amir recited to him:

*I know that I shall become a buried corpse,*
*when the travelling caravans set out, I shall not set out.*
*So the askers say, "For whom did you dig?"*
*And the informers say to them, "A vizier."*

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, we and our fathers have been promised this before. This is nothing but the fables of the ancients﴾ (23:83)**

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: They said, "We have indeed been promised this promise that you make us, O Muhammad, and our fathers were promised it before us by people who claimed that they were messengers of God before you, but we have never seen it in reality." ﴿This is nothing﴾ means: what you promise us of resurrection after death is ﴿nothing but the fables of the ancients﴾, meaning: what the ancients inscribed in their books of stories and reports, which have no authenticity or reality.

* *

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it, if you know?" They will say, "To God." Say, "Will you not then remember?"﴾ (23:84–85)**

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to these deniers of the Hereafter among your people: To whom belongs the dominion of the earth and of those in it of creation, if you know who its owner is? Then He informs him that they will acknowledge that it belongs to God as its sole possessor, to the exclusion of all other things besides Him. ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾ means: so say to them, when they answer you with that, "Will you not then remember?", so that you may know that whoever is able to create that from the beginning is able to bring them back to life after their death and to restore them as a sound creation after their annihilation.

* *

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne?" They will say, "To God." Say, "Will you not then fear Him?"﴾ (23:86–87)**

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say to them, O Muhammad: Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Throne that encompasses all of that? They will say: all of that belongs to God, and He is their Lord. So say to them: Will you not then fear His punishment for your disbelief in Him and your denial of His report and the report of His Messenger?

The readers (qurra') have differed regarding the recitation of His words ﴿They will say, "To God"﴾. The majority of the readers of Hijaz, Iraq and Sham recited it as ﴿sayaqūlūna lillāh﴾, except Abu 'Amr, who differed from them and recited it in this place as "sayaqūlūna Allāh" (without the lām), and in the next instance following it, in conformity with the script of the mushaf (the codified written copy of the Qur'an) — for that is how it is written in the mushafs of the cities — except in the mushaf of the people of Basra, where both instances are written with an alif. So they recited both with the alif, in conformity with the script of their mushaf. As for those who recited it with the alif, there is no difficulty in their recitation, because they treated the answer as a nominal sentence (beginning) and matched a nominative with a nominative. The meaning of the speech according to their recitation is: "Say: Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne? They will say: the Lord of that is God." So there is no difficulty in reciting it in this way. As for those who recited it without the alif in this instance and the one following it, they said: the meaning of His words "Say: Who is the Lord of the heavens?" is "To whom belong the heavens? To whom does the dominion of that belong?" So the answer was given in terms of meaning, and it was said "To God", because the question concerns to whom the dominion of that belongs. They said: this is like the saying of someone to a man: "Who is your master?", and the one answering responds to the meaning of what was asked, saying: "I belong to so-and-so", because what is understood from the answer is the same as what is understood from saying: "My master is so-and-so."

Some of them mentioned that a man of the Banu 'Amir recited to him:

*I know that I shall become a buried corpse,*
*when the travelling caravans set out, I shall not set out.*
*So the askers say, "For whom did you dig?"*
*And the informers say to them, "A vizier."*

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 23, verses 88–89:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: "In whose hand is the dominion (malakut) of everything, who gives protection while none can be protected against Him, if you know?" (88) They will say, "To Allah." Say: "Then how are you deluded?" (89)﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad: In whose hand are the treasuries of everything?

As related:

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah ﴿malakut of everything﴾: he said: the treasuries of everything.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿In whose hand is the malakut of everything﴾: he said: the treasuries of everything.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿and He gives protection﴾:

Whoever He wills to harm from among those who intend evil against him, ﴿and none can be protected against Him﴾ means: and no one can prevent from Him whoever He wills to harm, so as to ward off His punishment and retribution from him. ﴿If you know﴾ that such is His attribute. They will say that the malakut of everything and the power over all things belong to Allah. So say to them, O Muhammad: ﴿Then how are you deluded?﴾ They will say: In what manner are you turned away from believing in the signs of Allah, and from acknowledging His reports and the reports of His Messenger, and from believing that Allah is capable of everything He wills, and of resurrecting you alive after your death, while you know what you say of His great authority and power?

It is related from Ibn Abbas, concerning the meaning of His saying ﴿tus'harun (you are deluded)﴾, that he said:

* It was narrated to me by Ali, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Muawiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Then how are you deluded?﴾ he said: you are lying.

I have already explained earlier that sihr (magic) is the imagining of a thing to the observer as being other than what it actually is in its form. So the meaning of His saying ﴿Then how are you deluded?﴾ is only: in what manner is falsehood imagined to you as truth, and the corrupt as sound, so that you are turned away from acknowledging the truth to which Our Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) calls you?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 23, verse 90–92:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Nay, We have brought them the truth, and indeed they are liars (90). Allah has not taken any son, nor was there with Him any other god; for then each god would have taken away what he created, and some of them would have overpowered others. Glory be to Allah above what they describe (91). Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, so exalted is He above what they associate (with Him) (92).﴾

He says: The matter is not as these polytheists claim, that the angels are daughters of Allah, and that the gods and idols are deities besides Allah. ﴿Nay, We have brought them the truth﴾, meaning the certainty, which is the religion with which Allah sent His Prophet ﷺ, and that is Islam, and nothing is to be worshipped besides Allah, because there is no god but Him. ﴿And indeed they are liars﴾, He says: Indeed the polytheists are liars in what they attribute to Allah, and ascribe to Him of offspring and partners. As for His words: ﴿Allah has not taken any son﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Allah has no son, nor was there with Him in eternity, nor when He originated things, any one deserving of worship; and if there were with Him in eternity or at the creation of things any one deserving of worship ﴿besides Allah, then, for then each god would have taken away﴾, He says: then each god among them would have withdrawn ﴿what he created﴾ of any thing, and would have been alone with it, and they would have contended with one another, so that some of them would have overpowered others, and the stronger among them would have subdued the weaker; for the stronger would not be content that a weaker one should rise above him, and the weak is not fit to be a god. So glory be to Allah, how forceful and concise is this proof, for one who understands and reflects.

* *

As for His words: ﴿for then each god would have taken away﴾

It is the answer to an omitted clause, which is: If there were with Him a god, then each god would have taken away what he created; the omitted part is left out because what has been mentioned indicates it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Glory be to Allah above what they describe﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Exalting Allah above what these polytheists ascribe to Him, that He has a son, and above what they claim, that He has a partner, or that there is with Him in eternity a god worshipped, blessed and exalted is He.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: He knows what has been hidden from His creation of things, so they have not seen or witnessed it, and what they have seen and witnessed. This is from Allah a report about those polytheists who said, "Allah has taken a son," and worshipped besides Him gods, that in what they say and do they are falsifiers and in error, for they say what they say about this without knowledge, rather out of their ignorance of it. The One who knows the ancient and the recent affairs, and what is witnessed and unseen by them, is Allah, from whom nothing is hidden, so His report is the truth, not their report. And He said: ﴿Knower of the unseen﴾, in the nominative on the basis of an inceptive (mubtada'), meaning: He is the Knower of the unseen. That is why the fa' entered in His words ﴿so exalted is He﴾, as one says: "I passed by your brother the benefactor, so I did good to him," where you put "the benefactor" in the nominative when you make the statement with fa' ("so I did good to him"), because the meaning of the sentence in that case is: "I passed by your brother, he is the benefactor, so I did good to him." But if the sentence were made with waw, saying "and I did good to him," the proper case for "the benefactor" would have been only the genitive, as an epithet of "brother." Likewise, if ﴿and exalted is He﴾ came with waw, the proper case of ﴿Knower of the unseen﴾ would be the genitive, by following the case of the name of Allah, and the meaning of the sentence would be: "Glory be to Allah, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and exalted!" Then His words ﴿and exalted is He﴾ would be conjoined to "Glory be to Allah." It is permissible to use the genitive with fa' as well, since the Arabs may begin a sentence with fa' just as with waw, and Abu 'Amr would read ﴿Knower of the unseen﴾ in this place with the genitive, while the reading of the regional readers is otherwise.

The correct reading in this matter, in our view, is the nominative, for two reasons: first, the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it; and second, its soundness in Arabic.

* *

As for His words: ﴿so exalted is He above what they associate﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Allah is raised high and exalted above the polytheism of these polytheists, and above their description of Him by what they describe.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 23, verse 93–98:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "My Lord, if You should show me that which they are promised, (93) My Lord, then do not place me among the wrongdoing people." (94) And indeed, We are able to show you that which We promise them.﴾ (95)

Exalted is He, mentioning to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad: "My Lord, if You show me among these polytheists the punishment You promise them, then do not destroy me with what You destroy them with, and save me from Your punishment and Your wrath, and do not place me among the polytheist people, but make me among those with whom You are pleased, from among Your allies."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿then do not place me﴾

It is the response (jawab) to His saying: ﴿if You should show me﴾. Something was interposed between them, namely the vocative (nida'). Had there not been a conditional (jaza') before it, this would not be permissible in speech; one does not say: "O Zayd, then stand up," nor "O Lord, then forgive," because the vocative is a new (mustanif) clause, and likewise the imperative after it is a new clause, which does not take the fa' or the waw, unless it is a response to a preceding statement.

* *

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed me, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿And say: "My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the incitements of the devils"﴾, he said: The incitements of the devils are their strangling of people, and that is their hamazat.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they be present with me﴾

He says: And say, I seek Your protection, my Lord, lest they be present in my affairs.

Like what was said:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿And I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they be present with me﴾, in some matter of mine.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 23, verses 99–100:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "My Lord, send me back, that perhaps I may do righteousness in what I have left behind." No! It is only a word he is saying, and behind them is a barzakh until the Day they are resurrected.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Until, when death comes to one of these polytheists, and he witnesses the descent of God's command concerning him, he says (because of the great thing he witnesses of what he is about to face of God's punishment, in regret over what has passed and in anguish over what he neglected before that of obedience to God and asking Him for a reprieve): ﴿My Lord, send me back!﴾ That is, return me to the world. ﴿That perhaps I may do righteousness﴾ means: so that I may do righteousness in what I left behind before today of deeds, which I wasted and neglected.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Ma'shar, who said: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi used to recite to us: ﴿Until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "My Lord, send me back"﴾. Muhammad said: "To what does he wish to return? To what does he desire to return? * Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿My Lord, send me back﴾: "This is in the life of this world. Do you not see that He says: ﴿Until, when death comes to one of them﴾?" He said: "When the world comes to an end and he witnesses the Hereafter, before he tastes death."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 23, verse 101:

The exegetes differed concerning the referent of His words ﴿Then when the Horn is blown﴾ among the two blowings: which of them is meant by it. Some of them said: what is meant by it is the first blowing.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Hakkam ibn Salm related to us, he said: Amr ibn Mutarrif related to us, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that a man came to Ibn Abbas and said: I heard God say: ﴿there will be no kinship between them that day﴾ ... the verse, and He said in another verse: ﴿and they will turn to one another, questioning﴾. He said: As for His words ﴿there will be no kinship between them that day, nor will they question one another﴾, that is at the first blowing, so nothing will remain on the earth. ﴿There will be no kinship between them that day﴾... As for His words ﴿and they will turn to one another, questioning﴾, that is when they have entered Paradise, and they turn to one another, questioning.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu Ahmad related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His words: ﴿Then when the Horn is blown, there will be no kinship between them that day, nor will they question one another﴾, he said: at the first blowing.

Ali related to us, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿there will be no kinship between them that day, nor will they question one another﴾, that is when the Horn is blown, and no living being remains except God. ﴿And they will turn to one another, questioning﴾, that is when they are raised at the second blowing.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The meaning according to this interpretation is: when the Horn is blown, then whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will swoon, except whomever God wills. Then there will be no kinship between them that day through which they connect, nor will they question one another, nor visit one another, so that they ask about their conditions and their lineages.

Others said: rather, what is meant by it is the second blowing.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn Fudayl related to us, from Harun ibn Abi Wakī', he said: I heard Zadhan say: I came to Ibn Mas'ud while the people had gathered to him in his house, and I could not find a seat. I said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, is it because I am a man from the non-Arabs that you look down on me? He said: Come near! So I drew near, and there was no one sitting between me and him. He said: A male or female slave will be taken by the hand on the Day of Resurrection before the heads of the first and the last, and a herald will call out: Behold, this is so-and-so, son of so-and-so; whoever has a right against him, let him come to his right. He said: On that day a woman will rejoice that she has a right over her son, or her father, or her brother, or her husband. ﴿So there will be no kinship between them that day, nor will they question one another﴾.

Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Isa ibn Yunus related to us, from Harun ibn Anterah, from Zadhan, he said: I heard Ibn Mas'ud say: A male or female slave will be taken on the Day of Resurrection and set up before the heads of the first and the last; then a herald will call out, and he mentioned something similar, and he added in it: The Lord, blessed and exalted, will say to the servant: Give these people their rights. He will say: My Lord, the world has perished, so from where shall I give them? He will say to the angels: Take from his good deeds and give to every person according to the measure of his claim. If he has the weight of a mustard seed of surplus, God will multiply it for him until He admits him to Paradise by it. Then Ibn Mas'ud recited: ﴿Indeed, God does not wrong [anyone] an atom's weight; and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward﴾. And if he is a wretched servant, the angels will say: Our Lord, his good deeds have been exhausted and many claimants remain. He will say: Take from their evil deeds and add them to his evil deeds, and write out for him a certificate to the Fire.

Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, concerning: ﴿Then when the Horn is blown, there will be no kinship between them that day, nor will they question one another﴾, he said: No one on that day will ask anyone by lineage about anything, nor will they question one another, nor will anyone claim kinship with him through a womb relation.

Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Kathir related to me, from Hafs ibn al-Mughira, from Qatadah, he said: There is nothing more hateful to a person on the Day of Resurrection than to see someone who will dislike him, lest something of his sins be transferred to him. Then he recited: ﴿On the Day when a man will flee from his brother, and his mother and his father, and his spouse and his children, each man that Day will have a matter that occupies him﴾.

Al-Hasan related to us, he said: al-Hakam ibn Sinan related to us, from Sudus, companion of al-Sa'iri, from Anas ibn Malik, he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, a herald will call out from the people of the Throne: O people of wrongdoing, make amends for your wrongs, and enter Paradise."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 23, verses 102–104:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then whoever's scales are heavy, those are the successful. And whoever's scales are light, those are the ones who have lost their souls, abiding forever in Hell. The Fire burns their faces, and they therein are grim-faced.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿Whoever's scales are heavy﴾ — meaning the scales of his good deeds are heavy, and the scales of his evil deeds are light — ﴿those are the successful﴾, meaning: those who abide forever in the Gardens of Bliss. ﴿And whoever's scales are light﴾ — he says: and whoever's scales of good deeds are light, so that the scales of his evil deeds outweigh them — ﴿those are the ones who have lost their souls﴾ — he says: they have cheated themselves of their portion of Allah's mercy — ﴿abiding forever in Hell﴾ — he says: they are in the Fire of Hell.

* *

And His saying: ﴿The Fire burns their faces﴾

He says: the Fire scorches their faces.

As related:

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said regarding ﴿The Fire burns their faces﴾: "It scorches." ﴿And they therein are grim-faced﴾: al-Kulooh is that the two lips shrink back from the teeth until the teeth show, as al-A'sha said:

"And to him is the advance, none is like him, at the hour when the cheeks grimace from the fangs in a frown."[[This verse is by al-A'sha of Banu Qays ibn Tha'laba (his Diwan, p. 241, with the commentary of Dr. Muhammad Husayn, Cairo edition). The narration in it is "idha" in place of "la mithla lahu". Al-Muqaddam, with a damma on the mim, is a verbal noun meaning advancing. Kalah = al-shidq: he bared the fangs in a frown.

He praises Iyas ibn Qabisa al-Ta'i, saying that among his qualities is advancing in war when heroes dislike the fight, and their cheeks bare their fangs, hating war. The author cites it here to show that the meaning of al-kulooh is the lips shrinking back from the teeth until the teeth show.]] So the meaning of the statement is: the blaze of the Fire scorches their faces and burns them, and they therein have their lips drawn back from their teeth, from the burning of the Fire upon their faces.

The interpreters have said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to me, saying: Muawiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And they therein are grim-faced﴾: "They are scowling."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya and Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah, regarding His saying: ﴿And they therein are grim-faced﴾, he said: "Have you not seen the singed head, its teeth showing and its lips drawn back?"

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Israil, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah, that he recited this verse: ﴿The Fire burns their faces﴾ ... to the end of the verse, and said: "Have you not seen the head singed by fire, its lips drawn back and its teeth showing?"

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿And they therein are grim-faced﴾: "Have you not seen the sheep, when the fire touches their faces, how they are?"

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said regarding ﴿The Fire burns their faces﴾: "It scorches." ﴿And they therein are grim-faced﴾: al-Kulooh is that the two lips shrink back from the teeth until the teeth show, as al-A'sha said:

"And to him is the advance, none is like him, at the hour when the cheeks grimace from the fangs in a frown."[[This verse is by al-A'sha of Banu Qays ibn Tha'laba (his Diwan, p. 241, with the commentary of Dr. Muhammad Husayn, Cairo edition). The narration in it is "idha" in place of "la mithla lahu". Al-Muqaddam, with a damma on the mim, is a verbal noun meaning advancing. Kalah = al-shidq: he bared the fangs in a frown.

He praises Iyas ibn Qabisa al-Ta'i, saying that among his qualities is advancing in war when heroes dislike the fight, and their cheeks bare their fangs, hating war. The author cites it here to show that the meaning of al-kulooh is the lips shrinking back from the teeth until the teeth show.]] So the meaning of the statement is: the blaze of the Fire scorches their faces and burns them, and they therein have their lips drawn back from their teeth, from the burning of the Fire upon their faces.

The interpreters have said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to me, saying: Muawiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And they therein are grim-faced﴾: "They are scowling."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya and Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah, regarding His saying: ﴿And they therein are grim-faced﴾, he said: "Have you not seen the singed head, its teeth showing and its lips drawn back?"

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Israil, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah, that he recited this verse: ﴿The Fire burns their faces﴾ ... to the end of the verse, and said: "Have you not seen the head singed by fire, its lips drawn back and its teeth showing?"

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿And they therein are grim-faced﴾: "Have you not seen the sheep, when the fire touches their faces, how they are?"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 23, verses 105–106:

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Did not My verses used to be recited to you, and you used to deny them?﴾ ﴿They will say, "Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us, and we were a misguided people."﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: It will be said to them, ﴿Did not My verses used to be recited to you?﴾ meaning the verses of the Qur'an recited to you in the world, ﴿and you used to deny them?﴾ The phrase "it will be said" (yuqal) is omitted, as the context indicates it. ﴿They will say, "Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us"﴾.

The reciters differed over the reading of this. The reciters of Madina and Basra and some of the people of Kufa generally read ﴿ghalabat ʿalaynā shiqwatunā﴾ with a kasra on the shin and without an alif (shiqwah). The reciters of Kufa in general read "shaqawatunā" with a fatha on the shin and an alif.

The correct position regarding this is that both are well-known readings, and scholars among the reciters read each of them with the same meaning. Whichever of the two a reader recites is correct. The meaning of the statement is: they said, "Our Lord, what was decreed for us in Your prior knowledge and inscribed for us in the Mother of the Book overcame us."

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Hakkam narrated to us, from ʿAnbasa, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿our wretchedness overcame us﴾, he said: "That which was written against us."

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, he said: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿our wretchedness overcame us﴾, "that which was written against us."

al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Ibn Juraij said: We have been told that the people of the Fire called out to the keepers of Hell: "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment." They did not answer them for what God willed. When they answered them after a while, they said: ﴿So call; but the call of the disbelievers is only in error.﴾ He said: Then they called out to Malik: ﴿O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us﴾. Malik, the keeper of Hell, remained silent with them for forty years, then answered them, saying: ﴿Indeed you will remain.﴾ Then the wretched called to their Lord, saying: ﴿Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us, and we were a misguided people. Our Lord, bring us out of it; then if we return, we are indeed wrongdoers.﴾ He remained silent with them for a period equal to the duration of the world. Then, after that, the Blessed and Exalted answered them: ﴿Be driven away therein, and do not speak to Me.﴾

[The commentator notes: "Perhaps the speaker here too is al-Qasim, the narrator of the hadith with the preceding chain."] Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allah, he said: The people of the Fire call out to the people of Paradise, and they do not answer them for what God willed. Then it is said: Answer them, though they have cut off kinship and mercy. The people of Paradise say: "O people of the Fire, the wrath of God is upon you! O people of the Fire, the curse of God is upon you! O people of the Fire, no 'labbayk' nor 'sa'dayk' [welcome] to you! What do you say?" They say: "Were we not in the world your fathers, your sons, your brothers and your kin?" They say: "Yes." They say: ﴿Pour upon us some water, or some of what God has provided you.﴾ They answer: ﴿God has forbidden both to the disbelievers.﴾

[The commentator notes: "Perhaps the speaker here too is al-Qasim, the narrator of the hadith with the preceding chain."] Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Maʿshar, from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi, he said: ʿAbda al-Marwazi narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from ʿAmr ibn Abi Layla, he said: I heard Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, one of them adding to the other: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb said: It reached me, or it was mentioned to me, that the people of the Fire sought help from the guards: "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment." They replied to them with what God said. When they despaired, they called: "O Malik!" He was over them, having a seat in the middle of it, and bridges over which the angels of punishment pass; he sees its far end as he sees its near end. They said: "O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us," asking for death. He remained without answering them for eighty thousand years of the years of the Hereafter, or as he said. Then he descended to them and said: ﴿Indeed you will remain.﴾ When they heard that, they said: "Then be patient, perhaps patience will benefit us, as the people of the world were patient in obedience to God." He said: They were patient, and their patience lasted long, so they called: ﴿It is equal for us whether we are impatient or patient; we have no place of escape.﴾ That is, no deliverance. Then Iblis stood up and addressed them, saying: ﴿Indeed God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you. I had no authority over you.﴾ When they heard his speech, they loathed themselves. He said: They were called: ﴿The hatred of God is greater than your hatred of yourselves, when you were called to faith and you disbelieved.﴾ They said: ﴿Our Lord, You made us die twice…﴾ the verse. He said: God answers them: ﴿That is because when God alone was invoked you disbelieved, and when partners were associated with Him you believed. So judgment belongs to God, the Most High, the Great.﴾ He said: They say: "We have not yet despaired." Then they called a second time, saying: ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us; we will do righteousness, for we are certain.﴾ He said: The Lord, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿Had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance.﴾ The Lord says: Had I willed, I would have guided all people, and none of them would have differed. ﴿But the word from Me has come into effect: I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men together. So taste, for you forgot the meeting of this your day; indeed We have forgotten you. And taste the punishment of eternity for what you used to do.﴾ He said: They say: "We have not yet despaired." He said: They call a third time: ﴿Our Lord, delay us to a near term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers.﴾ He said: It is said to them: ﴿Did you not swear before that there would be no decline for you, and you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves?﴾ … the verse. He said: They say: "We have not yet despaired." Then they said again: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out; we will do righteousness other than what we used to do.﴾ He said: He says: ﴿Did We not give you life long enough for whoever would remember to remember, and the warner came to you?﴾ up to ﴿helper.﴾ Then He remained silent with them as long as God willed, then called to them: ﴿Did not My verses used to be recited to you, and you used to deny them?﴾ When they heard that, they said: "Now He will have mercy on us." At that they said: ﴿Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us⁠—that is, the Book that was written against us—and we were a misguided people. Our Lord, bring us out of it…﴾ the verse. Then He said: ﴿Be driven away therein, and do not speak to Me.﴾ He said: So they will never speak therein again, and at that point their supplication and hope ceased. Some of them began barking in the faces of others, and they were enveloped.

ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said in his narration: al-Azhar ibn Abi al-Azhar told me that he said: That is His word: ﴿This is a day when they will not speak, nor will they be given leave to make excuse.﴾

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allah, that he said: By Him who sent down the Qur'an upon Muhammad, the Torah upon Musa, and the Gospel upon ʿIsa, the people of the Fire say no word after that except the wailing and the roaring, forever in eternity, with no end to it.

He said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Maʿshar, who said: We were at a funeral with us Abu Jaʿfar the reciter; we sat, then Abu Jaʿfar withdrew and wept. He was asked: "What makes you weep, Abu Jaʿfar?" He said: Zayd ibn Aslam told me that the people of the Fire do not breathe.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And we were a misguided people﴾

It means: we were a people who strayed from the path of right guidance and the aim of truth.

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: "Our Lord, bring us out of it, and if we return, then indeed we are wrongdoers. He said, 'Be driven back into it, and do not speak to Me.'" (23:107–108)

His saying, the Exalted, mentioning the statement of those whose good deeds weighed light on the Day of Resurrection, in Hell: "Our Lord, bring us out of the Fire; and if we return, then indeed we are wrongdoers," meaning: if we return to what You dislike of deeds, then we are wrongdoers.

* *

As for His saying, "He said, 'Be driven back into it'":

His mention, may His remembrance be exalted, says: the Lord, may His praise be glorified, said to them in reply, "Be driven back into it," meaning: remain in the Fire. It is said of it: "Khasa'a (he drove away) so-and-so, yakhsa'uhu, khas'an and khusu'an"; and "khasi'a huwa, yakhsa'u," and "ma kana khasi'an," and "laqad khasi'a." "And do not speak to Me": at that, the wretched ones despaired of relief, though they had been hoping for it.

As related:

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, who said: Abu al-Za'ra' related to me, from Abdullah, in a narration he mentioned concerning intercession, he said: "When God wills not to bring anyone out of it (i.e., out of the Fire), except for their faces and their colours, a man from among the believers comes and intercedes for them, and says, 'O Lord!' He says, 'Whoever recognises anyone, let him bring him out.' So the man comes and looks, and does not recognise anyone, and says, 'O so-and-so, O so-and-so!' He says, 'I do not know you.' At that, they say: '﴿Our Lord, bring us out of it; and if we return, then indeed we are wrongdoers.﴾' He says: '﴿Be driven back into it, and do not speak to Me.﴾' When they say that, Hell closes over them, and no human being comes out of it."

* Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Ishaq informed us, from Sharik, from al-A'mash, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ma'di Karib, from Abu al-Darda', who said: "Hunger is sent down, or poured upon the people of the Fire, and it will equal what they are in of torment. So they cry for help, and are given relief with ḍarī' (a thorny plant), which neither fattens nor satisfies hunger. That does not avail them anything, so they cry for help again, and are given food with a choking throat. When they eat it, it sticks in their throats, and they recall that in the world they used to swallow choking food with water. So they cry for help, and boiling water is raised to them on iron hooks; when it reaches their faces it scorches their faces, and when they drink it, it cuts their bowels." He said: "Then they call out to Malik: 'Let your Lord decree against us.' He leaves them for a thousand years, then answers them: '﴿Indeed you will remain.﴾' Then they call out to the guardians of Hell: '﴿Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the torment.﴾' They say: '﴿Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs?﴾' They say: '﴿Yes.﴾' They say: '﴿Then call, but the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error.﴾' He said: 'They say, "We find no one better for us than our Lord," so they call upon their Lord: "﴿Our Lord, bring us out of it; and if we return, then indeed we are wrongdoers.﴾"' He said: 'Then God says: "﴿Be driven back into it, and do not speak to Me.﴾"' He said: 'At that, they despair of every good, and they begin to cry out with wailing, groaning and lamentation.'"

* Muhammad ibn Umarah al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: Asim ibn Yusuf al-Yarbu'i narrated to us, saying: Qutbah ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Asadi narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shamir ibn Atiyyah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Hunger is cast upon the people of the Fire..." and he then mentioned something similar.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Harun ibn Antarah, from Amr ibn Murrah, who said: "The people of the Fire see Malik, the guardian of the Fire, once every seventy years, and they say: '﴿O Malik, let your Lord decree against us﴾'. He answers them with a single word, and then they do not see him for seventy years. So they cry for help to the guardians, who say to them: '﴿Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the torment﴾'. They answer them: '﴿Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs...﴾' to the end of the verse. They say: 'Call upon your Lord, for no one is more merciful than your Lord.' They say: '﴿Our Lord, bring us out of it; and if we return, then indeed we are wrongdoers﴾'. He said: 'He answers them: "﴿Be driven back into it, and do not speak to Me﴾". At that they despair of every good, and they take up sighing, wailing and lamentation.'"

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning "﴿Be driven back into it, and do not speak to Me﴾", he said: "It has reached me that they call out to Malik and say: '﴿Let your Lord decree against us﴾'. He remains silent toward them for about forty years, then says: '﴿Indeed you will remain﴾'. Then they call out to their Lord, and He remains silent toward them for the length of the world twice over, then says: '﴿Be driven back into it, and do not speak to Me﴾'." He said: "The people then despair, and do not utter another word after that; there is only groaning and sighing." Qatadah said: "The voice of the disbeliever in the Fire is like the voice of a donkey: its beginning is zafir (a deep groan) and its end is shahiq (a sob)."

* Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, the like of it.

* Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Isa narrated to us, saying: Ziyad al-Khurasani informed me, saying: "He traced it to some of the people of knowledge, but I have forgotten (who), concerning His saying: '﴿Be driven back into it, and do not speak to Me﴾'," he said: "They fall silent, and no sound is heard there except like the ringing of a basin."

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: "﴿Be driven back into it, and do not speak to Me﴾": "This is the statement of the Most Merciful, mighty and majestic, when their speech to Him was cut off."

* *

As for His saying, "He said, 'Be driven back into it'":

His mention, may His remembrance be exalted, says: the Lord, may His praise be glorified, said to them in reply, "Be driven back into it," meaning: remain in the Fire. It is said of it: "Khasa'a (he drove away) so-and-so, yakhsa'uhu, khas'an and khusu'an"; and "khasi'a huwa, yakhsa'u," and "ma kana khasi'an," and "laqad khasi'a." "And do not speak to Me": at that, the wretched ones despaired of relief, though they had been hoping for it.

As related:

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, who said: Abu al-Za'ra' related to me, from Abdullah, in a narration he mentioned concerning intercession, he said: "When God wills not to bring anyone out of it (i.e., out of the Fire), except for their faces and their colours, a man from among the believers comes and intercedes for them, and says, 'O Lord!' He says, 'Whoever recognises anyone, let him bring him out.' So the man comes and looks, and does not recognise anyone, and says, 'O so-and-so, O so-and-so!' He says, 'I do not know you.' At that, they say: '﴿Our Lord, bring us out of it; and if we return, then indeed we are wrongdoers.﴾' He says: '﴿Be driven back into it, and do not speak to Me.﴾' When they say that, Hell closes over them, and no human being comes out of it."

* Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Ishaq informed us, from Sharik, from al-A'mash, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ma'di Karib, from Abu al-Darda', who said: "Hunger is sent down, or poured upon the people of the Fire, and it will equal what they are in of torment. So they cry for help, and are given relief with ḍarī' (a thorny plant), which neither fattens nor satisfies hunger. That does not avail them anything, so they cry for help again, and are given food with a choking throat. When they eat it, it sticks in their throats, and they recall that in the world they used to swallow choking food with water. So they cry for help, and boiling water is raised to them on iron hooks; when it reaches their faces it scorches their faces, and when they drink it, it cuts their bowels." He said: "Then they call out to Malik: 'Let your Lord decree against us.' He leaves them for a thousand years, then answers them: '﴿Indeed you will remain.﴾' Then they call out to the guardians of Hell: '﴿Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the torment.﴾' They say: '﴿Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs?﴾' They say: '﴿Yes.﴾' They say: '﴿Then call, but the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error.﴾' He said: 'They say, "We find no one better for us than our Lord," so they call upon their Lord: "﴿Our Lord, bring us out of it; and if we return, then indeed we are wrongdoers.﴾"' He said: 'Then God says: "﴿Be driven back into it, and do not speak to Me.﴾"' He said: 'At that, they despair of every good, and they begin to cry out with wailing, groaning and lamentation.'"

* Muhammad ibn Umarah al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: Asim ibn Yusuf al-Yarbu'i narrated to us, saying: Qutbah ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Asadi narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shamir ibn Atiyyah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Hunger is cast upon the people of the Fire..." and he then mentioned something similar.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Harun ibn Antarah, from Amr ibn Murrah, who said: "The people of the Fire see Malik, the guardian of the Fire, once every seventy years, and they say: '﴿O Malik, let your Lord decree against us﴾'. He answers them with a single word, and then they do not see him for seventy years. So they cry for help to the guardians, who say to them: '﴿Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the torment﴾'. They answer them: '﴿Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs...﴾' to the end of the verse. They say: 'Call upon your Lord, for no one is more merciful than your Lord.' They say: '﴿Our Lord, bring us out of it; and if we return, then indeed we are wrongdoers﴾'. He said: 'He answers them: "﴿Be driven back into it, and do not speak to Me﴾". At that they despair of every good, and they take up sighing, wailing and lamentation.'"

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning "﴿Be driven back into it, and do not speak to Me﴾", he said: "It has reached me that they call out to Malik and say: '﴿Let your Lord decree against us﴾'. He remains silent toward them for about forty years, then says: '﴿Indeed you will remain﴾'. Then they call out to their Lord, and He remains silent toward them for the length of the world twice over, then says: '﴿Be driven back into it, and do not speak to Me﴾'." He said: "The people then despair, and do not utter another word after that; there is only groaning and sighing." Qatadah said: "The voice of the disbeliever in the Fire is like the voice of a donkey: its beginning is zafir (a deep groan) and its end is shahiq (a sob)."

* Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, the like of it.

* Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Isa narrated to us, saying: Ziyad al-Khurasani informed me, saying: "He traced it to some of the people of knowledge, but I have forgotten (who), concerning His saying: '﴿Be driven back into it, and do not speak to Me﴾'," he said: "They fall silent, and no sound is heard there except like the ringing of a basin."

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: "﴿Be driven back into it, and do not speak to Me﴾": "This is the statement of the Most Merciful, mighty and majestic, when their speech to Him was cut off."

**Commentary on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted:** ﴿Indeed, there was a group of My servants who used to say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of the merciful."﴾ (23:109)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿Indeed﴾. This *hā'* in His words "innahu" is the *hā'* that the grammarians call *al-hā' al-majhūla* (the "unspecified hā'," a pronoun whose referent is not stated, which the grammarians call *ḍamīr al-sha'n*). I have already explained its meaning earlier. Its purpose in the speech, with what has made its repetition unnecessary in this place, is: ﴿there was a group of My servants﴾, meaning: there was a company of My servants, who are the people of faith in God, who used to say in this world: ﴿"Our Lord, we have believed"﴾ in You, in Your messengers, and in what they brought from You, ﴿"so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of those who show mercy to the afflicted, so do not punish us with Your punishment."﴾
