Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on surah 23, verse 111:

On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So you took them in mockery until they made you forget My remembrance, and you used to laugh at them. Indeed, I have rewarded them today for their patience; indeed, they are the triumphant.﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: You took them, O you who said to your Lord, ﴿Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us, and we were a misguided people﴾ in the world, and who said therein, ﴿Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of the merciful﴾, as objects of mockery (sukhriyyan). The ha' and mim in His words ﴿fa-ittakhadtumuhum﴾ refer to the group.

The reciters differed over the reading of His words ﴿sukhriyyan﴾. Some reciters of the Hijaz and some of Basra and Kufa read ﴿sikhriyyan﴾ with a kasra on the sin, and in justifying the kasra they interpret its meaning as ridicule (al-huzu'). They say that if it is read with a damma, the word means servitude and enslavement (al-sukhrah wa'l-isti'bad). So the meaning of the statement according to these scholars is: you took the people of faith in Me in the world as objects of derision and play, mocking them, until they made you forget My remembrance. Most reciters of Medina and Kufa read ﴿sukhriyyan﴾ with a damma on the sin, and they said the meaning of the word is the same with the damma and the kasra. Some of them reported from the Arabs, by hearing, lijji and lujji, and dirri and durri (relating to pearl, al-durr), and likewise kirsi and kursi; and they said this is from their usage in this manner, like their saying in the plural of 'asa (staff): al-'isi with a kasra on the ayn and al-'usi with a damma on it. They said: We have chosen the damma in sukhri only because it is the more eloquent of the two dialects.

The correct view on this matter is that both are well-known readings and two recognized dialects with one meaning. Scholars among the reciters have read each of them, so whichever of the two the reciter reads is correct. No one is known to distinguish in meaning between the word when the sin is read with a kasra and when it is read with a damma, based on the transmission from those who heard from the Arabs what I have reported from them.

Mention of the transmission with its chain from some of those who distinguished between its meaning with a kasra on the sin and with a damma on it:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding ﴿fa-ittakhadtumuhum sikhriyyan﴾: They are two different words: sikhriyyan and sukhriyyan. God says: ﴿And We raised some of them above others in rank, that some of them may take others in service (sukhriyyan)﴾. He said: This is sikhriyyan: they subjugate them; and the others, who mock them, are sukhriyyan, so sikhriyyan is those who subjugate them in your sight, and subjugation (taskhir) is your raising yourself above them; and the others, who mock the people of Islam, are sukhriyyan: they mock them. So the two are different. He recited the saying of God: ﴿And whenever a chief of his people passed by him, they mocked him. He said: If you mock us, indeed we mock you as you mock﴾, and he said: they mock them as the people of Noah mocked Noah. ﴿fa-ittakhadhuhum sukhriyyan﴾: they took them as objects of ridicule (huzu'), and they never ceased mocking them.

* *

On His words ﴿until they made you forget My remembrance﴾:

He says: Your continuous mockery of them made you forget, by what you did to them, My remembrance, and it diverted you from it. ﴿And you used to laugh at them﴾.

As follows:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿until they made you forget My remembrance﴾: Their mockery of them and their laughing at them made these people forget God. He recited: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed﴾, up to His words ﴿Indeed, these are misguided﴾.

* *

On His words ﴿Indeed, I have rewarded them today for their patience﴾:

He, exalted is His mention, says: Indeed I, O polytheists who are eternal in the Fire, have rewarded those whom you took in the world as objects of mockery from among the people of faith in Me, and at whom you laughed today, for their patience upon what they endured among you from the harm of your mockery and your laughter at them in the world. ﴿That they are the triumphant﴾.

The reciters differed over the reading of "innahum" (that they). The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of Kufa, read "annahum" with a fath on the alif of "anna-hum," meaning: I have rewarded them this (the victory). So the anna in their reading is in the accusative position, governed by the verb "jazaytuhum" (I rewarded them). Their meaning is: I rewarded them today with the triumph of Paradise. It may also be accusative in another respect, that it is directed to mean: I rewarded them today for their patience, because they are the triumphant for their patience in the world, upon what they encountered for the sake of God. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read "innī" with a kasra on the alif, in the sense of a new beginning (ibtida'), and they said that is a new beginning from God praising them.

The more correct of the two readings is the reading of the one who reads with a kasra on the alif, because His words "jazaytuhum" have governed the ha' and mim, and the verb of recompense governs two objects. If it governs the ha' and mim, it cannot also govern "anna," which would make it govern three; unless it is intended as a repetition, in which case the accusative of "anna" would be by a hidden verb, not by "jazaytuhum." If "anna" were put in the accusative by a hidden lam (in order that), it also would not have much meaning, because God's recompense of His believing servants with Paradise is only on account of their good deeds in the world, and His recompense to them, which in the Hereafter is the triumph, so there is no sense in stipulating for them triumph through deeds and then informing that they triumphed only because they are the triumphant.

Thus the interpretation of the statement, since the correct reading is what we have mentioned, is: I have rewarded them today with Paradise for their patience in the world upon your harm to them, in that they are today the triumphant with everlasting bliss and eternal honor, for the good deeds they performed in the world and for the hardships they encountered in seeking My pleasure therein.

The commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿He will say, "How many years did you remain on the earth?" (112) They will say, "We remained a day or part of a day; so ask those who count."﴾ (113)

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words ﴿How many years did you remain on the earth?﴾ and His words ﴿We remained a day or part of a day﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra, and some of the people of Kufa, recited it in the form of a statement: ﴿He said, "How many years did you remain?"﴾, and likewise His words ﴿He said, "How long did you remain?"﴾. The reasoning of these readers is that the meaning of the discourse is that Allah said to these wretched people of the Fire, while they were in the Fire: ﴿How many years did you remain on the earth?﴾, and that they answered Allah saying: ﴿We remained a day or part of a day﴾. The wretched forgot the length of their stay in the world because of the great affliction and punishment they were in, and the span of their stay in it seemed short to them because of the vengeance of Allah that had befallen them, until they thought that they had not remained in it except a day or part of a day. Perhaps some of them had remained in it a long time and many years.

The majority of the readers of Kufa recited it in the form of a command to them to speak, as if He had said to them: "Say, how long did you remain on the earth?" He put the speech in the form of a command addressed to one person, while meaning a group, since its meaning was understood. The reason those from Kufa who chose this reading chose it is that in their codices it reads "Qul" (say) without an alif, while in other codices it has an alif.

The most correct of the two readings is the reading of the one who recited: ﴿He said, "How many years did you remain?"﴾ in the form of a statement. This is because, if the discourse were a command, it would be "qulu" (say) in the plural form of address, since the address in what comes before and after it is directed to the group of the people of the Fire. Therefore, it is more fitting that it be so if the speech came in the form of a command. Although the other form, namely the singular, is permissible, for the reason I have explained to the reader of it, and since the speech came with the singular in the reading of all the readers, it is known that reciting it as a statement about the singular is more similar, since that is the eloquent and well-known usage of the Arabs. If that is the case, the interpretation of the speech is: Allah said, "How many years did you remain in the world?" They answered Him saying: "We remained in it a day or part of a day, so ask those who count, for we do not know; we have forgotten it."

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of "those who count" (al-ʿaddin). Some of them said: they are the angels who guard the deeds of the children of Adam and count their hours upon them.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, he said: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿so ask those who count﴾: He said: the angels.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

Others said: rather, they are the calculators (al-Hussab).

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada: ﴿so ask those who count﴾, he said: ask the calculators.

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada: ﴿so ask those who count﴾, he said: ask the people of calculation.

The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say as Allah, mighty is His praise, said: ﴿so ask those who count﴾, and they are those who count the number of months, years and other things. It is permissible that they be the angels, and it is permissible that they be the children of Adam and others; there is no proof for either, by which of them its soundness is established, and it is not permissible to direct the meaning to some of those who count to the exclusion of others.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 23, verses 114–115:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿He will say, "You remained not but a little, if only you had known."﴾ [23:114]

The reciters differed over the reading of His words ﴿He will say, "You remained not but a little"﴾, just as they differed over the reading of His words ﴿"How many years did you remain?"﴾ [23:112]. Our view on this point is the same as the view we set out earlier concerning His words ﴿How many years did you remain?﴾. The meaning of the statement, according to our reading, is: God says to them, "You remained on earth only a little, a small amount of time, if only you had known the measure of your stay there."

* *

And His words: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose [ʿabath], and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ [23:115]

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Did you think, O wretched ones, that We created you, when We created you, for play (laʿib) and vanity (bāṭil), and that you would not return to your Lord after your deaths, to live again, so that you would be recompensed for what you used to do in the world?

The reciters differed over the reading of this. Some reciters of Madina, Basra and Kufa read ﴿turjaʿūn﴾ with a dammah on the tā', i.e. ﴿turaddūn﴾ (you will be brought back), and said: it refers only to the return (marjiʿ) of the Hereafter, not to a return to the world. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read ﴿tarjiʿūn﴾ with a fatḥah on the tā', and said: the return of the Hereafter and the return to the world are the same in this respect.

The most correct of these opinions, in our view, is to say: they are two readings close in meaning, because whoever God returns from the world to the Hereafter after his annihilation has indeed returned to it, and whoever returns to it, by God's returning him to it, has returned. Moreover, they are both well-known readings, and scholars among the reciters have read each of them, so whichever one the reader recites is correct.

In accordance with what we have said about the meaning of His words ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose?﴾, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose?﴾, he said: "Vanity (bāṭil)."

Those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose?﴾, he said: "Vanity (bāṭil)."

The interpretation of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿So exalted is God, the True King. There is no god but Him, the Lord of the Noble Throne.﴾ (23:116)

He, may He be remembered, says: So exalted is God, the True King, above what these polytheists attribute to Him, that He has a partner, and above what they ascribe to Him of taking daughters. ﴿There is no god but Him﴾ means: there is no deity worthy of worship except God, the True King. ﴿The Lord of the Noble Throne.﴾ The word "al-Rabb" (the Lord) is in the nominative (marfu', the grammatical case of the subject), by way of a qualifier that refers back to "al-Haqq" (the True). The meaning of the sentence is: So exalted is God, the True King, the Lord of the Noble Throne; there is no god but Him.

* *

The interpretation of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And whoever calls upon another god along with God, for which he has no proof, then his account is only with his Lord. Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed.﴾ (23:117)

He, may He be remembered, says: Whoever calls upon another deity alongside the One whose worship is alone fitting, as if it were a god, has no argument for what he says and does in this regard, and no evidence.

As follows:

He related to me, Muhammad ibn 'Amr, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us. And al-Harith told me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿for which he has no proof﴾, he said: "evidence."

He related to us, al-Qasim, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid: ﴿for which he has no proof﴾, he said: "argument."

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Hakkam related to us, from 'Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿for which he has no proof﴾, he said: "no argument."

* *

As for His words: ﴿then his account is only with his Lord﴾

He says: his account for his evil deeds is only with his Lord, who will repay him his recompense when he comes before Him. ﴿Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed﴾ means: indeed, those who disbelieve in God will not prosper before Him, nor will they attain eternity and everlasting survival in bliss.

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And say: "My Lord, forgive and have mercy, and You are the best of the merciful"﴾ (118)

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And say, O Muhammad: "My Lord, cover over my sins by Your pardon of them, have mercy on me by accepting your repentance, and by Your leaving off punishing me for what I have committed," ﴿and You are the best of the merciful﴾. He says: And say: "You, O my Lord, are the best of those who show mercy to one who has sinned, so that He accepts his repentance and does not punish him for his sin."

End of the commentary on Surah al-Mu'minun.
